Ezeiruaku's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 22.

10913.short: Porter (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
10913.long: Porter was unable to play against the Colts in Week 9 due to an ankle injury, and he posted a DNP-DNP-LP practice log for Week 10 prep. DaRon Bland (ankle) is also listed as questionable, and the next options available for outside cornerback are Cobie Durant, Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel.

8476.short: Bland (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
8476.long: Bland first appeared on Friday's practice report as a limited participant, which indicates that he injured his ankle during that session. That's not a good sign for Bland heading into the weekend, and the Cowboys could be without both of their starting outside cornerbacks depending on the status of Joey Porter (ankle), who is also listed as questionable. Cobie Durant, Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel are the top candidates to start at outside cornerback if one or both of Bland or Porter were to miss time.

10225.short: Mingo (ankle/foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
10225.long: Mingo was held out of practice all week while recovering from foot and ankle injuries that he picked up during the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts in Week 9. In his absence, KaVontae Turpin -- who is returning from a three-game absence due to a rib injury -- and Camden Brown are both in line for a slight uptick in offensive snaps. Mingo's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 22.

8917.short: Turpin (ribs) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
8917.long: Turpin has missed the Cowboys' last three games while recovering from a rib injury that he suffered in Week 6 against the Packers. His return will bolster Dallas' special teams, as he is the top returner on kickoffs and punts, and he'll also give the offense a boost as an explosive playmaker.

8137.short: Pickens (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
8137.long: After being listed as limited on five consecutive injury reports going back to last week due to a hamstring issue, Pickens practiced fully Friday and thus is set to miss just one game as a result. In eight appearances so far this season, he's talled a 39-533-2 line on 62 targets.

9227.short: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that Abanikanda likely will be promoted from the practice squad to replace Tyler Goodson (knee) as the No. 2 running back ahead of Sunday's matchup with San Francisco, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
9227.long: A 2024 fifth-round pick, Abanikanda has six regular-season appearances and 29 career touches -- all back in 2023 for the Jets. He offers sub-4.5 speed at 215-plus pounds, but he won't necessarily have the same role as Goodson, who earned the team's trust with solid performances after latching on earlier this fall. With Abanikanda as the No. 2 back, Javonte Williams may be tasked with even larger workloads than before.

10933.short: Overshown (hamstring/back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
10933.long: Overshown didn't play in the Week 9 win over the Colts. He was limited in Wednesday's practice, though after logging a full session Thursday, he is good to go for Sunday's meeting with the 49ers. The 26-year-old has appeared in only three games during the 2026 campaign, amassing 20 total tackles (eight solo) and one interception.

13376.short: Downs recorded three tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass breakups, including an interception, in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
13376.long: Squaring off with his older brother Josh Downs on the opposite side, Downs recorded his first career interception on the Colts' final offensive play of the game with 41 seconds left in the fourth quarter. On a pass intended for Keenan Allen, Downs picked off Daniel Jones to seal the four-point win. The first-round rookie Downs now has 55 tackles (32 solo), including 2.0 sacks, three pass breakups, with the interception, and a pair of forced fumbles on 93 percent of the defensive snaps across nine starts this season.

10871.short: Schoonmaker (groin) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
10871.long: The tight end has missed the past two games for Dallas, but appears to be ready to return and could see significant snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford while Jake Ferguson (knee) is sidelined.

13496.short: The Cowboys designated Moore (hip) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
13496.long: The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.

8207.short: Goodson sustained ACL and MCL sprains in his knee during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, a source tells Todd Archer of ESPN.com.
8207.long: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer already confirmed Monday that Goodson would be sidelined for multiple weeks due to the injury, and now that details have emerged regarding the severity of the issue, it's conceivable that the 26-year-old could be headed for injured reserve. The loss of Goodson leaves the Cowboys with no healthy running backs on the active roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but team owner Jerry jones said that the team plans to sign a free-agent back Tuesday, per Archer. Dallas also has Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin as backfield options on the practice squad.

11783.short: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
11783.long: Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

11593.short: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts.
11593.long: Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the season thus far, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine contests.

6419.short: Locke (concussion) won't play in Sunday's game against the 49ers, Patrik Walker of the team's official site reports.
6419.long: Locke suffered a concussion in Week 8 versus the Cardinals. While he was cleared to play in Week 9 against the Colts, he suffered another concussion. Now, Locke will miss at least one game, though the team will presumably be overly cautious before allowing him to get back on the field, meaning Markquese Bell may be in line for more snaps.

8110.short: According to coach Brian Schottenheimer, Ferguson (knee) is in line to miss multiple weeks, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
8110.long: At a minimum, Ferguson is on track to miss at least this coming weekend's game against the 49ers, but a 'multiple week' timetable hints at a possible IR stint for the tight end. Next up for the Cowboy's reps at the position are Brevyn Spann-Ford, Luke Schoonmaker (groin) -- when healthy -- and James Mitchell. With the NFL trade deadline arriving Tuesday, it's also not difficult to imagine Dallas looking into gaining additional help in Ferguson's looming absence.

11533.short: Aubrey went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
11533.long: Aubrey was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game, but he did miss a kick for the second straight week. The kicker had makes from 45 and 28 yards in the contest, but he continued his long-range struggles Sunday, pulling a 50-yard attempt wide left late in the fourth quarter. Aubrey has now gone 17-for-22 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests to open the 2026 campaign.

3294.short: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
3294.long: Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

7588.short: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
7588.long: Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.

6786.short: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
6786.long: Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the 49ers next Sunday.

11017.short: Winters (head) has returned to Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
11017.long: Winters was evaluated for a concussion earlier in the second half but was ultimately cleared to return. That's a big boost to Dallas' defense, especially since fellow linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back) was unable to suit up Sunday.

2617.short: Singleton recorded six tackles (two solo) during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers in Week 9.
2617.long: Singleton's six stops were a season low, but he still finished second on the Broncos in that category behind Jahdae Barron (eight). It's been a career year for Singleton, who is up to an NFL-leading 107 total tackles through nine regular-season games, which includes 2.0 sacks.

6869.short: Trautman caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
6869.long: Trautman failed to record a catch across six games between Weeks 2 and 7, but he has logged two receptions in each of his two outings. His 41 offensive snaps ended up being ahead of fellow tight end Evan Engram (38), although the latter has been more involved in the Broncos' offensive game plan than Trautman. The Broncos' next game takes place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22.

9494.short: Mims caught one of two targets for zero yards, added a five-yard carry and returned three punts for 22 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
9494.long: Nineteen of Mims' 24 snaps came on offense, although he logged only two touches in the process. He hasn't seen more than four targets in a game this season, with most of his output coming on special teams as a returner on both kickoffs and punts. The Broncos are on a bye for Week 10, so their next game will take place in Week 11 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 22

11627.short: Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
11627.long: Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

4066.short: Engram caught four of five targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
4066.long: The four catches matched Engram's season high, and his 33 yards were his most since Week 5. It goes without saying, but Engram is well off the fantasy radar at tight end. He has 17 catches for 169 yards and one touchdown through nine games, averaging a career-low 18.8 yards per contest.

3678.short: Lutz went 2-for-2 on both his field-goal attempts and extra-point tries during Denver's win over Carolina on Sunday.
3678.long: Lutz's field-goal tries were good from 26 and 48 yards. The 32-year-old has now converted 16 of his 19 field-goal attempts and all 16 of his extra-point tries across nine appearances this season.

6806.short: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
6806.long: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

12492.short: Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
12492.long: Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

5045.short: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
5045.long: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

13345.short: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
13345.long: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

11563.short: Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries.
11563.long: The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

7526.short: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
7526.long: After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.

10930.short: Moss (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
10930.long: Moss has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Jahdae Barron will likely finish the game at outside cornerback for the Broncos.

12427.short: Tillman is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
12427.long: Tillman was on the injury report ahead of the Week 9 meeting with Carolina due to a hamstring issue. However, he will avoid his second absence of the 2026 campaign. The 28-year-old has appeared in seven games for the Broncos this season, amassing 19 total tackles (10 solo).

8347.short: The Broncos placed Uwazurike (shoulder) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
8347.long: Uwazurike wasn't able to practice at all this week due to a shoulder issue. He started seven of Denver's first eight games, but he's now required to miss the team's next four contests. Third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim could see the first gameday action of his career as a result.

6868.short: Wonnum (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
6868.long: Wonnum entered the league's concussion protocol during the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. He was held out of Detroit's Week 9 win over Miami, but Wonnum has cleared protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return bolsters the Lions' rotational depth on the defensive line alongside Aidan Hutchinson, Tyler Lacy and Derrick Moore.

11729.short: Vaki (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
11729.long: Vaki played through the same injury last week, taking five touches for 21 yards in a 19-9 win over the Dolphins. He didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday this week, but a return to practice Friday puts him on track to avoid the inactive list ahead of Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. If Vaki doesn't end up playing, Jacob Saylors will step into the No. 2 RB role behind workhorse Jahmyr Gibbs.

7547.short: St. Brown (ribs) was a limited participant in Friday's practice and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Germany, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
7547.long: St. Brown played through the same injury (and same 'questionable' tag) last week, catching eight passes for 86 yards on a team-high 10 targets in Detroit's 19-9 win over Miami. He'll likely play again, but fantasy managers will want to make sure of it when the Lions release their inactive list at 8:00 a.m. ET on Sunday. St. Brown has been a limited participant in every practice since first injuring his ribs in a Week 8 win over Minnesota.

10905.short: Branch (hip) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
10905.long: Branch upgraded his practice status to full participation after beginning the week limited. The 25-year-old has 14 tackles (seven solo) and one interception in three regular-season games.

5372.short: Reed (hip) did not travel to Munich with the Lions and is ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Patriots.
5372.long: Reed did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a hip injury suffered late in Week 8. Rock Ya-Sin and Ennis Rakestraw could see extended playing time for the second straight week in Reed's stead. Reed has 42 tackles (29 solo) and seven pass deflections, including one interception, in seven regular-season games.

8348.short: Joseph (knee) did not travel to Munich with the Lions and is ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Patriots.
8348.long: Joseph was a full participant in practice Thursday, but it appears the Lions are taking a cautious approach to his return. The 25-year-old has one more chance to return from the reserve/PUP list in Week 11 before he becomes ineligible for the remainder of the season.

3163.long: Goff kicked off Week 10 prep as limited Wednesday due to a chest injury, but his return to all activity one day later puts him in the clear for Sunday's contest against the Patriots in Munich. He'll be taking on a New England defense that was just torched by Packers QB Jordan Love for 372 yards and three touchdowns in Week 9.

4224.short: Clark registered five tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins in Week 9.
4224.long: Clark jumped in front of a Malik Willis (abdomen) deep pass intended for Caleb Douglas early in the third quarter, which the Lions offense converted into a 33-yard field goal by Jake Bates eight plays later. It was Clark's second interception of the season and first since Week 1 against the Saints. The veteran safety is up to 49 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble through eight regular-season games.

11237.short: Saylors (neck) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
11237.long: Saylors sat out his first game of the season in Week 9 due to a neck injury, but it now looks like he's on track to return to game action in Week 10. With teammate Sione Vaki tending to an ankle issue, it appears possible Saylors could be called upon for a larger share of offensive snaps than usual versus the Patriots.

12535.short: TeSlaa registered one catch for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 19-9 win over Miami.
12535.long: Jared Goff threw to TeSlaa twice on Detroit's opening drive but didn't turn to him again for the remainder of the contest. The second-year wideout thus continued a very unproductive stretch, as he's logged just two catches for 19 yards on six targets over his past four games. TeSlaa is still working as Detroit's No. 3 wideout -- among Lions wide receivers, only Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown logged more offensive snaps Sunday -- but looks just aren't coming his way. He'll try to break out of the funk next Sunday against New England.

10859.short: The Lions have received trade calls on LaPorta leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the team prefers to keep him with the hope of signing the tight end to a long-term deal, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
10859.long: Earlier in the season, LaPorta expressed his frustration with the Lions for the organization's inability to come to terms on an extension with him, but both sides still appear to be on good terms and willing to re-engage in discussions on a new deal before he becomes a free agent in 2027. The fourth-year tight end has likely helped his case for earning a lucrative contract by having thus far stayed healthy throughout the season while putting together a 35-399-3 receiving line on 49 targets over the Lions' first eight games.

7698.short: The Lions acquired Cisco from the Jets on Monday in exchange for a 2029 sixth-round pick, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
7698.long: Cisco will now suit up for his third NFL team after spending time with the Jaguars and Jets since entering the league in 2021. He had served mainly as a special-teams contributor over his final six games with Jacksonville, but Cisco should see more playing time on defense for a leaky Detroit secondary.

11539.short: Bates went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 19-9 win over the Dolphins.
11539.long: Bates was able to make multiple field goals for the third straight game after having done so just once over the team's first five contests this year. The kicker converted attempts from 28 and 40 yards in the first half before adding makes from 33 and 43 yards after the break. Bates has now gone 16-for-17 on field-goal tries while making all 24 of his PATs over eight games during the 2026 campaign to this point.

8148.short: Williams brought in one of two targets for 31 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
8148.long: Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

9221.short: Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
9221.long: It was a relatively quiet day by Gibbs' lofty standards against a Dolphins team that's proven to have plenty of fight despite its losing record. The standout back salvaged his fantasy day with an eight-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, Gibbs' second score on the ground in as many games and ninth overall. Gibbs failed to record at least one reception for the first time this season, but he's already amassed 1,132 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns across eight games heading into next Sunday's showdown against the Patriots in Germany.

10880.short: The Lions moved Campbell (neck) to injured reserve Saturday.
10880.long: Campbell suffered a neck injury while making a tackle in the third quarter of last Sunday's win over Minnesota and remains in the hospital. Detroit head coach Dan Campbell shared Friday that the linebacker continues to improve, but  his placement on IR means he'll miss at least the team's next four games. K.J. Britt, who Detroit signed off New England's practice squad Wednesday, may be asked to immediately step into a starting role.

13494.short: Rolder (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
13494.long: This move was anticipated, as Rolder suffered a season-ending hamstring injury in the Lions' win over Minnesota on Sunday. The rookie linebacker logged a career-high 17 defensive snaps and notched his first NFL sack in that contest, so his injury comes at an unfortunate time. Rolder will now turn his focus toward rehabbing the injury in order to be ready for offseason activities in 2027.

8303.short: McCreary (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
8303.long: McCreary wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday but practiced in a limited capacity Friday. As a result, the 26-year-old was listed as questionable for the divisional showdown with Minnesota, though he has since been cleared to suit up. McCreary has appeared in all six of Detroit's regular-season games in 2026, amassing 22 total tackles (17 solo), 1.0 sacks and one forced fumble.

11689.short: Rakestraw (ankle) does not have a game designation for Sunday's Week 8 tilt versus the Vikings.
11689.long: Rakestraw suffered an ankle injury late in this past Sunday's win over Green Bay. He was held to limited practice sessions Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday. As such, Rakestraw is good to go for Sunday's big battle against Minnesota.

8205.short: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Pacheco (back) has a chance to return in late December, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
8205.long: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

11712.short: Hopper (illness) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
11712.long: Hopper started Week 10 prep with consecutive limited sessions before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's practice. The inside linebacker appears to be over his illness and is all set to suit up for Sunday's divisional clash with the Vikings.

10885.short: Van Ness (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
10885.long: Van Ness logged a limited practice Friday after consecutive DNPs to start Week 10 prep. The linebacker could suit up for Sunday's game if his back feels better by game day. If Van Ness ends up inactive for the NFC North showdown, Brenton Cox and Dani Dennis-Sutton are set to split snaps across from Barryn Sorrell.

11686.short: Bullard (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
11686.long: Bullard was a non-participant in consecutive sessions to start Week 10 prep before upgrading to limited in Friday's practice. The slot cornerback now has a chance to suit up for Sunday's game, but with just one practice under his belt, it is more likely that Kamal Hadden takes over the role against the Vikings.

5346.short: Franklin (shin) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
5346.long: Franklin was a non-participant throughout the Packers' Week 10 prep, but the linebacker has not yet been officially ruled out ahead of Sunday's divisional contest. If Franklin is inactive come game time, Isaiah McDuffie is in line to take over as the starting inside linebacker opposite Ty'Ron Hopper.

10212.short: Whyle (concussion) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
10212.long: Whyle missed all of the Packers' Week 10 prep due to a concussion. The tight end remains in the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest, leaving Mark Redman and Jonnu Smith as the depth options behind Tucker Kraft.

8168.short: Moore (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
8168.long: Moore has remained on IR since suffering an ankle injury in Week 5. The wide receiver logged limited practice sessions throughout Week 10 prep but likely will not be elevated for Sunday's contest, as the Packers are set to allocate any additional roster space to the running back position in Josh Jacobs' (finger) absence.

11370.short: Brooks (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
11370.long: Brooks logged three consecutive limited practices during Week 10 prep as he works his way back from an ankle injury he suffered in Week 4 that landed the running back on IR. With Josh Jacobs (finger) ruled out for Sunday's divisional contest, Brooks could be activated ahead of Sunday's game to play alongside MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson.

6788.short: McKinney (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
6788.long: McKinney was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a foot injury. His late addition to the practice report isn't a good sign, and McKinney is now in jeopardy of missing his first game due to injury since the 2022 campaign, when he was a member of the Giants. Kitan Oladapo and Kamal Hadden would be the top candidates to start at safety alongside Evan Williams if McKinney is unable to play Sunday.

12482.short: Williams (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
12482.long: Despite being listed as limited on all three of the Packers' Week 10 practice reports due to a groin injury, Williams has been cleared for Sunday's matchup. In his four appearances this season, he's turned his 19 touches (11 catches, eight rushes) into 153 yards from scrimmage and one receiving touchdown.

7640.short: Parsons (knee/illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
7640.long: Parsons now has put together back-to-back weeks of limited sessions as he inches closer to his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. With a Week 11 bye on tap, he'll have a bit more time to get healthy before the Packers' Week 12 road matchup with the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, which coincides with his 21-day practice window coming to a close.

12704.short: Coach Matt LaFleur said Thursday that he expects Brinson (IR, calf) to play again at some point this season, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
12704.long: Brinson suffered a calf injury during the preseason that forced him to miss the Packers' first three regular-season games before he was ultimately sent to injured reserve in early October. LaFleur also said Thursday that Brinson is recovering from a groin surgery, which could be a factor in his extended absence. Until he comes back from IR, Anthony Campbell figures to continue to see increased reps on the defensive line in his stead.

8204.short: Melton (head) was removed from the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against Minnesota, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
8204.long: Melton exited the Week 9 win over the Patriots due to a possible concussion. However, with his omission from Thursday's edition of the injury report, he's good to go for Sunday's divisional showdown with the Vikings. The 27-year-old hasn't had a productive 2026 campaign, catching just five passes (10 targets) for 34 yards.

13545.short: Smack (calf) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
13545.long: Smack was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury. Head coach Matt LaFleur anticipated the kicker would practice without limitations Thursday, and that's exactly what happened, clearing the way for his availability in Week 10 against Minnesota. Smack is coming off a solid performance, making all three field-goal attempts while converting each of his four extra-point tries in the Packers' Week 9 victory over the Patriots.

5850.short: Jacobs will undergo finger surgery Friday, and the Packers will have a better sense of his recovery timetable afterward, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
5850.long: Jacobs exited Green Bay's Week 9 win over the Patriots after fracturing his ring finger and is in line to be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings. A more precise recovery timeline is expected to be established after Jacobs undergoes surgery on the injured finger Friday, though initial estimates put his likely absence at 2-to-3 weeks on the optimistic side. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are currently available to handle Green Bay's backfield duties while Jacobs is sidelined, plus Chris Brooks (ankle) is a candidate to return from IR as soon as this weekend.

11739.short: Williams logged five tackles (four solo) and one interception during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.
11739.long: Brandon Cisse broke up a deep pass from Drake Maye to Kyle Williams early in the second quarter, and Williams was able to make a toe-tapping grab for the takeaway. Williams is up to three interceptions on the year, which ties his career high that he set across 16 regular-season games in 2025. The third-year defensive back is up to 76 tackles (48 solo), including 1.0 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

7782.short: McDuffie registered 10 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.
7782.long: McDuffie's first tackle of the game was a nine-yard sack on Drake Maye early in the first quarter, which led to the Patriots punting the ball away on the next play. McDuffie also recovered the fumble he forced late in the third quarter, which the Packers offense turned into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Christian Watson one play later. McDuffie has racked up double-digit stops in three consecutive games, and he's been the starting inside linebacker in each of those contests due to the absence of Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie should hang onto his starting role against the Vikings on Sunday assuming Franklin is ruled out for that game.

11581.short: Lloyd (knee) is not listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday.
11581.long: The running back appears ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Vikings after missing Week 9 against New England. With Josh Jacobs (finger) set to miss some time, Lloyd figures to be part of the backfield mix, joining Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong.

4144.short: Smith didn't log a target or touch in a 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
4144.long: Jordan Love threw for a massive 372 yards in the victory, but Smith wasn't targeted on any of the quarterback's 29 passes. That's been par for the course this season -- Smith has drawn one or zero targets in five straight appearances. The veteran tight end has had some productive offensive seasons in his career, but it appears Smith isn't going to be a big part of the Packers' passing-game plans this year.

8116.short: Strong rushed eight times for 22 yards in Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots. He added two catches for 11 yards on two targets.
8116.long: With Josh Jacobs (finger) knocked out of the game in the first quarter and set to miss several weeks, Strong figures to see his role expand in Green Bay's backfield, though MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and even Chris Brooks (ankle) are likely to also see snaps in the coming weeks. Strong is not a recommended fantasy target in 12-team leagues.

12504.short: Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
12504.long: After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.

8406.short: Blankenship (concussion/hand) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Browns.
8406.long: Blankenship ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back full practices, and he's progressed enough through the league's concussion protocol to be cleared to play Sunday. He is also working through a left hand injury that required surgery in October, but that won't prevent him from playing against Cleveland. Blankenship's return means M.J. Stewart will revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

10892.short: Anderson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns.
10892.long: Anderson was added to Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. He was held out of Friday's session, but that may have been a precautionary measure to prevent an injury aggravation. Danielle Hunter (hamstring) already has been ruled out, so the Texans would have to rely on Jadeveon Clowney, Dominique Robinson and Sabastian Harsh as the top defensive ends if Anderson cannot play Sunday.

2393.short: Hunter (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
2393.long: Hunter popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. He was unable to practice Friday, and the injury is severe enough for him to miss his first game of the 2026 regular season. The Texans could also be without fellow star edge rusher Will Anderson (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game despite also sitting out of Friday's practice. Jadeveon Clowney, Dominique Robinson and Sabastian Harsh will all see more defensive snaps in the absence of Hunter, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against Indianapolis on Thursday.

7568.short: Jordan (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
7568.long: Jordan was unable to practice all week while tending to a finger injury, and his absence Sunday means Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover are all in line for more snaps on offense behind starting tight end Dalton Schultz. Jordan's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

6485.short: Al-Shaair (groin/personal) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
6485.long: Al-Shaair was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury and a personal matter, although it's unclear which issue is the bigger reason why the veteran linebacker will be sidelined for Sunday's road contest. Wade Woodaz and Jake Hummel (groin) -- the latter of whom is on injured reserve -- are the top candidates to start alongside Henry To'oTo'o and Jake Hansen at linebacker. Al-Shaair's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

9502.short: Dell (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Browns, while teammate Marvin Harrison (hamstring) has been ruled out.
9502.long: Last week, Dell caught four passes for 104 yards and a TD in a 44-22 win over the Chargers, leading Houston in targets (nine) in his second game back from a lengthy absence. His snap share (45 percent) and route share (55 percent) were less encouraging, but Dell and Kayshon Boutte are candidates for more playing time with Harrison out for at least one week.

11628.short: Harrison (hamstring) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
11628.long: Harrison's absence leaves more snaps for some combination of Xavier Hutchinson, Kayshon Boutte and Tank Dell, all of whom were productive last week in a win over the Chargers. C.J. Stroud has been spreading the ball around and putting up big numbers in the process, with even Nico Collins seeing his target share suffer as a result. Harrison is unlikely to handle a full-time role even when he gets back to full strength.

12474.short: Following a full practice Friday, Marks (knee) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Browns.
12474.long: After experiencing knee discomfort Wednesday and not practicing Thursday due to lingering soreness from hits, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, Marks worked fully to close the practice week and heads into the weekend without any availability concerns. Marks has seen the bulk of Houston's backfield work of late, but he may have some competition for carries Sunday, as David Montgomery (groin) -- who hasn't played since Week 5 -- practiced fully Friday and is listed as questionable to face Cleveland.

5892.short: Montgomery (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, while Woody Marks (knee) doesn't have an injury designation.
5892.long: Montgomery returned to practice Thursday after missing a month, and he upgraded from limited participation to full for Friday's practice. It's still not clear he'll be active ahead of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday, so Marks could be tasked with a heavy workload for a fifth straight game. If Montgomery does return, he'll likely share work with Marks, making it difficult to trust either Houston RB in fantasy lineups.

12626.short: The Texans designated Smith (hamstring) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
12626.long: Smith landed on injured reserve in early October due to a hamstring injury. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session. Smith would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Browns.

8733.short: The Texans opened Hummel's (groin) 21-day practice window Wednesday.
8733.long: Hummel was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and it was encouraging to see him back on the field after recovering from groin surgery. The Texans face the Browns on Sunday, but Hummel would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for that contest.

7585.short: Mills completed one of two pass attempts for seven yards and lost two yards on two carries in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
7585.long: Since the Texans had built their lead to 19 with less than five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach DeMeco Ryans opted to pull starting quarterback C.J. Stroud from the game and handed the offense over to Mills. In what marked his first playing time of the season, Mills directed two possessions. He led the Texans to a field goal with 2:20 remaining, then knelt twice to run out the clock when Houston got the ball back with 1:07 left. With Stroud enjoying a bounce-back campaign, Mills' opportunities will likely be limited to garbage-time situations if Stroud stays healthy.

11599.short: Stover was a healthy inactive for Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
11599.long: Week 9 marked the first time all season that Stover sat out, with the Texans opting to keep their other four tight ends (Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Brevin Jordan and Marlin Klein) active ahead of him. Through the Texans' first seven games, Stover had played less than half of the offensive snaps in each contest and recorded three receptions for 17 yards on five targets while rushing three times for five yards.

5985.short: Moreau didn't log any targets or touches Sunday in a 44-22 win against the Chargers.
5985.long: For the second straight week, Moreau didn't make a mark in the box score. He did technically draw a target (which he didn't catch), but it was wiped out by an accepted defensive penalty. Moreau hasn't had more than two catches in any game this season and has finished with fewer than 10 yards in every contest since Week 3, so he's not a viable fantasy play in virtually any format right now.

3451.short: Fairbairn went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made all five of his PATs during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
3451.long: Fairbairn was able to convert multiple field-goal attempts for the fifth straight game. The kicker made a 56-yarder in the first quarter before later adding makes from 31 and 41 yards in the fourth quarter. On the season, Fairbairn has gone 18-for-19 on field-goal tries, including 7-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far.

5001.short: Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
5001.long: Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

9504.short: Boutte erupted for four catches (on five targets) for 125 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 44-22 road win against the Chargers.
9504.long: Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.

10218.short: Hutchinson caught three of five targets for 29 yards and a touchdown and  added a 28-yard kick return during Sunday's 44-22 win against the Chargers.
10218.long: Hutchinson finished tied with Kayshon Boutte for second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Tank Dell (nine). Hutchinson was able to reach paydirt for the second straight contest, reeling in a 17-yard touchdown pass from C.J. Stroud for the team's first score of the day in the first quarter. There are many mouths to feed in Houston's passing attack, so Hutchinson will remain a volatile fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with the Browns.

7569.short: Collins corralled all four of his targets for 55 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 44-22 victory at the Chargers.
7569.long: Collins was one of four Texans to reach the end zone via a pass from QB C.J. Stroud, who tossed five TDs in all. It marked Collins' first touchdown since Week 4, when he struck twice against the Cowboys, but overall his output from week to week this season has been a bit inconsistent, as he sits on a 28-384-4 line on 39 targets through his six appearances. He'll seek better results next Sunday in Cleveland.

11777.short: Carlies (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
11777.long: Carlies exited the first half of the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys with a neck injury and did not return to the contest. The linebacker was unable to practice at all during Week 10 prep and has not progressed in his recovery. Austin Ajiake is set to be the backup middle linebacker to CJ Allen in Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

6129.short: Tillery (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Miami, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
6129.long: Tillery was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury before being sidelined both Thursday and Friday. Tim Smith and Kevin Givens are in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Tillery, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

10220.short: Mallory (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Miami.
10220.long: Mallory was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. His late addition isn't a great sign heading into the weekend, and with Mo Alie-Cox (groin) already ruled out, the Colts would turn to both Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown to step into larger roles behind Tyler Warren if Mallory is also sidelined.

6860.short: Davis-Gaither (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
6860.long: Davis-Gaither is set to miss a second consecutive game due to a knee injury that he likely picked up during the Colts' Week 8 loss to the Jaguars. His next chance to play is Thursday against the Texans, although Davis-Gaither was unable to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Jaylon Carlies (neck) is ruled out for Sunday's contest, so Austin Ajiake figures to be the top candidate to start alongside Bryce Boettcher and CJ Allen at linebacker, with Tahj Chambers providing depth at the position.

4054.short: Alie-Cox (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
4054.long: Alie-Cox suffered a groin injury during the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, and that injury prevented the veteran tight end from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Will Mallory (hamstring) is listed as questionable, so the Colts may have to rely more heavily on Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown to provide depth at tight end behind starter Tyler Warren for Sunday's contest. Alie-Cox's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

13384.short: Haulcy (ankle) was a full participant at Thursday's practice.
13384.long: Haulcy missed the Colts' Week 9 loss to Dallas due to an ankle injury and sat out practice Wednesday, but his return without limitations Thursday suggests the rookie third-round pick is ready to return to action. He's poised to reclaim the starting strong safety role Sunday against the Dolphins.

13388.short: Allen recorded 10 tackles (three solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
13388.long: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) out versus Dallas, Allen played all 79 defensive snaps for Indy, marking the first time the second-round rookie has played 100 percent of the defensive snaps in a game. He's started back-to-back contests and is up to 25 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and the one pass breakup across six appearances this season.

13481.short: Boettcher recorded 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
13481.long: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) inactive against Dallas, Boettcher saw a spike in playing time alongside CJ Allen at linebacker for the Colts. The fourth-round rookie Boettcher played a season-high 73 percent of the defensive snaps and recorded his first career game with double-digit tackles.

12723.short: Wohler recorded 16 tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
12723.long: With A.J. Haulcy (ankle) inactive, Wohler made the spot start alongside Cam Bynum at safety for the Colts. Wohler played 98 percent of the defensive snaps against Dallas, easily a new career-high playing-time clip for the second-year safety after he missed his entire rookie season with a foot injury. Once Haulcy returns, Wohler will likely return to a reserve and special-teams role.

12625.short: Walley (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
12625.long: After being injured in Week 7, Walley has missed the past two games but appears ready to return to the lineup Sunday against the Dolphins. He's spent most of his time covering the slot for the Colts this season, recording 35 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass breakups across seven appearances.

12518.short: Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports.
12518.long: The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.

13333.short: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
13333.long: A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is also on the roster.

5067.short: The Colts are opening Key's (hamstring) 21-day practice window, Joel A. Erickson of The Indianapolis Star reports.
5067.long: Key hasn't played since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Commanders. Now, after five weeks, the 30-year-old may begin practicing. He will likely need to string together multiple positive practices for a chance to play in Week 10.

8142.short: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
8142.long: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

6427.short: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Dulin will be one of the Colts receivers tasked with absorbing the snaps vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
6427.long: Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.

11762.short: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Gould is in line to step into the slot role previously held by Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
11762.long: With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.

3155.short: Treadwell logged 52 of the Colts' 64 snaps and was held without a reception on one target in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
3155.long: Since drawing a season-high eight targets in a Week 5 loss to the Steelers, Treadwell has barely surpassed that total over the past four games combined. Despite handling snap shares north of 70 percent in each of those contests, Treadwell has mustered a 5-58-0 receiving line on 10 targets during that stretch. The Colts will have more target volume up for grabs after trading Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday, and though Treadwell could be one of the beneficiaries, he still looks to be a low-upside fantasy option.

7496.short: The Colts signed Westbrook-Ikhine off their practice squad Tuesday.
7496.long: Indianapolis will turn to Westbrook-Ikhine to fill the 53-man roster spot vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday. Westbrook-Ikhine had previously been elevated from the Colts' practice squad for three straight games between Weeks 3 and 5 and failed to corral his lone target while logging 18 total snaps on offense. He'll fill a depth role in the Colts' receiving corps and could end up providing most of his value on the team's coverage and return units on special teams.

6813.short: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
6813.long: In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

12471.short: Giddens was active but didn't play in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
12471.long: Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.

12910.short: Green (forearm) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
12910.long: Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

8265.short: Walker (ribs) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
8265.long: Walker played through a rib injury during the Jaguars' win over the Ravens in Week 9. The defensive end sat out Wednesday's practice session to nurse the issue before logging consecutive limited practices to end Week 10 prep. Walker is set to once again play through the nagging injury in Sunday's divisional showdown with the Titans.

10219.short: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
10219.long: Rodriguez was listed as a limited practice participant all week,  but his hand issue is something he'll play through, while working alongside Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who returned to a limited session Friday and was also cleared for Week 10 action. Rodriguez has 55 carries in eight games to date, while Tuten has logged 122 rushes in that span, but Rodriguez has at least helped out his fantasy managers of late by scoring in each of his last two contests.

5947.short: Myers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
5947.long: Meyers has fought through one injury or another for most of the season. This week, he managed limited practices Thursday and Friday, setting him up to play against the last-place Titans.

12490.short: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
12490.long: Tuten played through the injury last week without practicing, and he'll now suit up for Week 10 after just one limited practice Friday. Chris Rodriguez (hand) also is cleared to play and could help ease the burden if Jacksonville is wary of overworking Tuten while he's banged up.

5017.short: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Friday that Bates and DT Jordan Davis will not play in Sunday's game at Tennessee, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
5017.long: Prior to being traded, Bates and Davis each made nine appearances for teams with late-season byes. The Jaguars had theirs in October, so Bates and Davis might've been looking at 18 straight weeks of action ahead of the playoffs. This ensures they'll get a week off and have more time to get comfortable with DC Anthony Campanile's scheme.

11631.short: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
11631.long: After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.

4207.short: The Jaguars acquired Godchaux from the Saints on Monday in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, though the selection could turn into a 2027 sixth-round pick if "conditions are met," Jonathan Jones of The Athletic of The Athletic reports.
4207.long: Godchaux was selected by Miami in the fifth round of the 2017 NFL Draft. Since then, he has appeared in 145 regular-season games for the Dolphins, Patriots and Saints, garnering 487 total tackles (224 solo), 5.5 sacks and three forced fumbles. Godchaux's presence will bolster depth at the defensive tackle position for the Jaguars, especially with DaVon Hamilton (knee) done for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

5332.short: Oluokun recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 33-10 victory over Baltimore.
5332.long: Oluokun tied for his team's lead in stops and notched his second sack of the season when he brought down Joe Fagnano early in the second quarter. Oluokun has been a reliable fantasy IDP asset in 2026 with at least seven tackles in six of his eight games so far. He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.

13408.short: Koziol finished Thursday's 33-10 win over Baltimore with two catches for 15 yards on two targets.
13408.long: Koziol was part of a three-tight-end starting unit for Jacksonville alongside Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher. Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.

13299.short: Boerkircher hauled in two of three targets for 61 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over Baltimore.
13299.long: Boerkircher was tied with Parker Washington for the second-most receiving yards on the team with 61. This game marks the fourth time this season that the rookie has surpassed 30 snaps on offense. Boerkircher has made a name for himself as Jacksonville's No. 2 option at tight end behind Brenton Strange.

13394.short: Cameron caught his only target for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 victory over the Ravens.
13394.long: Cameron didn't see the ball until the fourth quarter despite playing the third most snaps at wide receiver (25) for the Jaguars on Thursday, behind only Parker Washington (38) and Jakobi Meyers (38). This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.

2359.short: Abdullah carried the ball seven times for 30 yards and returned one kickoff for 24 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
2359.long: Abdullah recorded the third-most-offensive snaps in the backfield (seven), behind Chris Rodriguez (25) and Bayshul Tuten (20). Should everyone in the backfield remain healthy, Abdullah will likely see a similar workload for the rest of the season.

9480.short: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
9480.long: The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

12530.short: Hunter caught his only target for minus-1 yard and lost a fumble in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
12530.long: Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.

11786.short: Little made all four of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries in a 33-10 win over Baltimore on Thursday.
11786.long: The Jaguars dominated in the victory, but they fell short of the end zone enough times to keep Little busy. He didn't need to fully flex the strength of his leg, as his longest kick was from a modest 47 yards out, but Little extended his run of consecutive successful FG attempts to 10. He's now gone 14-of-16 on field-goal tries this season while converting 25 of 26 point-after attempts.

7523.short: Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while rushing once for minus-1 yard in the Jaguars' 33-16 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
7523.long: Lawrence unsurprisingly didn't have a high-volume night, as the Jaguars were progressively able to take control of the game with Joe Fagnano under center for the Ravens. The veteran signal-caller hit Parker Washington on a 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown over the middle just before halftime for his one scoring pass, and Lawrence connected with eight different targets overall on the night. The 2021 first overall pick has now thrown for 1,932 yards with an 18:4 TD:INT and added 79 yards on the ground heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

9487.short: Washington secured two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. He also returned one punt for 11 yards.
9487.long: Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

13390.short: Woods (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons.
13390.long: Woods will miss consecutive games due to a neck injury he sustained early in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder is progressing in his recovery, but it remains unclear when he will return to the field.

13419.short: Ott (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
13419.long: Ott popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. He was also limited in Friday's session, and with Kenneth Walker (groin) also questionable, the Chiefs enter the weekend with Emmett Johnson as the only healthy running back on the 53-man roster. Nate Carter is the only running back on Kansas City's practice squad and would be a top candidate for elevation to the active roster depending on the statuses of both Ott and Walker.

13385.short: Delane (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Atlanta.
13385.long: Delane has missed the Chiefs' last two games while recovering from a shoulder injury. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 10 prep, but that evidently wasn't enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's road game. Kristian Fulton and Christian Roland-Wallace would continue to operate in elevated roles in the secondary if Delane is not cleared to return.

4046.short: Mahomes (elbow) was a full practice participant throughout the week and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Atlanta.
4046.long: Mahomes made a quick return to last week's game after he was injured, and he'll make the start this Sunday against a Falcons defense that just lost safety Jessie Bates (traded to Jacksonville). The Chiefs, meanwhile, traded for wide receiver Josh Downs, who is expected to play Sunday, per coach Andy Reid. Starting right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) is ruled out, and running back Kenneth Walker (groin) is listed as questionable. The Chiefs may need more from Mahomes if Walker ends up inactive or limited.

8151.short: Walker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
8151.long: Walker was added to the Chiefs' Week 10 injury report due to groin tightness that kept him from practicing Friday. Now that he's carrying an official 'questionable' designation heading into the weekend, the running back's status will need to be tracked as Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff approaches. In the event that Walker -- who is averaging a robust 109.0 rushing yards per game and has scored 11 total TDs through eight contests -- is made inactive for the contest,  Emmett Johnson would be in line to handle the bulk of the team's carries versus Atlanta.

9500.short: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Friday that Downs looks ready to play in Sunday's game at Atlanta, Charles Goldman of AtoZ Sports reports.
9500.long: The Chiefs traded for Downs on Tuesday before the deadline and had him on the practice field by Wednesday. Reid stopped short of saying Downs will play, but it sounds like the wideout will have some kind of role this Sunday alongside Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy.

13337.short: Coach Andy Reid noted that Johnson would take the bulk of the Chiefs' carries in the event that Kenneth Walker -- who didn't practice Friday due to groin tightness -- is forced to miss Sunday's game against the Falcons, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.
13337.long: Added context regarding Walker's status will arrive via Friday's final injury report when the Chiefs assign their Week 10 injury designations. Chances are, Walker will be deemed questionable, but if he ends up sidelined this weekend, Johnson would provide those who roster Walker, or otherwise need RB help, with a viable pivot option.

3558.short: Jones recorded four tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
3558.long: The 32-year-old defensive lineman had gotten off to a slow start to begin the 2026 season, his 11th in the league. Prior to Sunday, he'd recorded just 0.5 sacks across the first seven games, so his 2.0 sacks were his first full ones of the campaign. Jones is now up to 17 tackles (eight solo), including 2.5 sacks, three pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 72 percent of the defensive snaps.

8385.short: Karlaftis recorded six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
8385.long: After starting the season without a sack in his first four games, Karlaftis has 4.0 sacks over his last four contests. For the season, the 25-year-old edge rusher is up to 32 tackles (16 solo), including the 4.0 sacks, a career-high nine pass breakups, including his first career interception, and a forced fumble across eight games. He's on pace to shatter his previous career high of 48 tackles, which was set last season.

7648.short: Bolton recorded 12 tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
7648.long: Bolton doesn't do much in the box scores other than rack up tackles, but he's good at that and now has five double-digit tackles games through eight contests to begin the 2026 campaign. For the season, Bolton is up to 80 tackles (39 solo), two pass breakups and a forced fumble on 99 percent of the Chiefs' defensive snaps.

6141.short: Tranquill collected 13 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
6141.long: It was Tranquill's second double-digit tackles game of the season, and both have come over the last three weeks. The veteran linebacker has piled up 66 tackles (33 solo), two pass breakups and one fumble recovery on 88 percent of the defensive snaps across eight games this season.

11624.short: Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City.
11624.long: Worthy was considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets in the fourth quarter. A quick return to full practice participation suggests Worthy will be fine for the upcoming matchup with Atlanta on Sunday, but his target share may decline in the second half of the season after Kansas City traded for WR Josh Downs.

4227.short: Butker will remain Kansas City's kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
4227.long: On that topic, coach Andy Reid said Wednesday, "I'm gonna stick with Butker this week." While the veteran kicker has held on to the top job through the Chiefs' first eight games, he's had accuracy issues this season, having converted 12 of his 19 field-goal attempts and making 22 of his 23 extra-point tries in that span. Reid's comment about Butker on Wednesday implies that the team's kicking situation is being evaluated on a weekly basis. Justin Tucker is on Kansas City's practice squad, and he remains an option should Reid decide that a switch is in order down the road.

7591.short: Fields carried twice for minus-one yard and lost a fumble while logging five snaps on offense in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
7591.long: The Chiefs' backup quarterback saw the field for just the second time this season, after he had previously played one snap in a Week 1 win over the Broncos.
