Due to head coach Andy Reid's reluctance to use starter Patrick Mahomes on quarterback sneaks, Fields subbed into the game for a third-and-1 play in the first quarter. Fields ended up coughing the football, with the Jets making the recovery. The Chiefs went on to build enough of a lead to rest Mahomes for the final possession of the game with just over two minutes left in the fourth quarter, when Fields proceeded to hand the ball off three times before kneeling to run out the clock.

12505.short: Royals caught both of his targets for 18 yards Sunday in a 35-12 rout of the Jets.
12505.long: Royals ranked fourth among KC wideouts in offensive snaps (21), trailing Xavier Worthy (49), Rashee Rice (38) and Andrew Armstrong (22). Royals matched his season high with two catches, and the 18 receiving yards were his second-most in a game this season. That speaks to the minimal production he's provided thus far, and Royals' role could be further reduced with the Chiefs' acquisition of Josh Downs on Tuesday.

7828.short: Gray caught his only target for 11 yards Sunday in a 35-12 win against the Jets.
7828.long: Gray was a minor factor in the passing game, with his lone reception gaining 11 yards late in the third quarter. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Travis Kelce paced Kansas City with 72 receiving yards on four catches. Gray had a nice two-game run with a combined six catches for 97 yards across Weeks 6 and 7, but since then he's tallied just three receptions for 26 yards and a touchdown across his subsequent two games.

13413.short: Allen failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
13413.long: Allen made the start at wide receiver but ran just 13 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 36 dropbacks against New York. With Xavier Worthy (hamstring) now injured, Allen could have a path to more playing time moving forward, but all three of Rashee Rice, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce are well ahead of the rookie wideout for targets.

10229.short: Rice secured five of seven targets for 49 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
10229.long: Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.

1466.short: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard.
1466.long: Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

8380.short: Booker (ankle) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
8380.long: Booker remains questionable despite upgrading to a full participant in Friday's practice session. The defensive lineman is likely a game-time decision, and if he is inactive for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, JJ Pegues will likely see more defensive snaps.

12541.short: Thornton (back) is questionable to play against the Seahawks on Sunday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
12541.long: Thornton was unable to practice Friday due to a back injury that he likely picked up at some point during Week 10 prep. His late addition to the injury report isn't a good sign for his availability Sunday, although he has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026, mostly due to a hamstring injury that landed him on injured reserve in late August.

5090.short: Fatukasi (shoulder/back) was a full participant at practice Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
5090.long: Fatukasi popped up on the Raiders' injury report Wednesday with shoulder and back issues, but it seems like those were minor, and he's in line to suit up in Week 10. He figures to start on the defensive line Sunday versus the Seahawks.

13398.short: Stukes registered five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
13398.long: Stukes jumped in front of a Brock Purdy pass intended for George Kittle midway through the third quarter, although the Raiders' offense gave the ball right back to the 49ers two plays later on a Brock Bowers fumble. It was the second interception of the season for Stukes, who was a second-round selection of the Raiders in the 2026 NFL Draft. The rookie out of Arizona is up to 43 tackles (23 solo) and four pass defenses through the first eight regular-season games of his NFL career.

7016.short: Chinn recorded nine tackles (six solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
7016.long: Chinn finished Week 9 as the Raiders' third-leading tackler behind Nakobe Dean (19) and Quay Walker (11). Dean has logged at least seven stops in five consecutive outings, and he has accumulated 66 tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception), two forced fumbles and two fumble recoveries over nine regular-season games.

8266.short: Walker posted 11 tackles (three solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
8266.long: It was the second time in three games that Walker finished with double-digit stops, and he finished second on the Raiders in tackles behind Nakobe Dean (19). Walker is on track for his fifth consecutive 100-plus tackle campaign and is up to 72 stops (28 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

8267.short: Dean logged 19 tackles (seven solo) during the Raiders' 38-17 loss to the 49ers in Week 9.
8267.long: Dean played every defensive snap and was all over the field in Week 9, finishing with a career-best 19 total tackles. He's logged at least 12 tackles in six of his last seven outings, and through nine regular-season games he has accumulated 98 total tackles, which is second-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107).

10866.short: O'Connell moves to QB No. 2 on the depth chart behind Fernando Mendoza, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
10866.long: O'Connell is set to back up rookie Mendoza, who replaced recently traded Kirk Cousins as the starting quarterback. O'Connell has been with Las Vegas since the team drafted him in the fourth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. The 28-year-old last appeared in a regular-season game in 2025, completing 10 of 22 attempts for 102 yards.

12483.short: Bech caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to the 49ers.
12483.long: Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.

13269.short: Mendoza will take over as the Raiders' new starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game versus the Seahawks after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota on Tuesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
13269.long: The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft has opened his professional career on the bench, with his lone action to date coming during garbage time of a blowout loss to the Patriots in Week 5, when he completed six of eight pass attempts for 48 yards. However, with the 4-5 Raiders shipping out Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick, the 23-year-old Mendoza will now be thrust into his first extended NFL playing time and will face a pair of tough defenses off the bat, as he'll follow up the matchup against the Seahawks with a road game in Denver in Week 11. Mendoza had underwhelming numbers over his three preseason appearances, but he's reportedly been "tearing it up in practice" during the regular season and has given the Raiders optimism that he's ready to lead the offense, per Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com.

6083.short: Gay converted his only field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during Las Vegas' loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
6083.long: Gay's lone field goal came from 50 yards in the second quarter, and he now has made three of his four kicks from 50 yards or longer on the season. The 32-year-old is 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 21-for-21 on extra-point tries across nine appearances.

8180.short: Nailor caught two of four targets for nine yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
8180.long: Nailor was a non-factor on offense in Week 9, failing to reach double-digit receiving yards for the fourth time this season. The wide receiver has had a hard time getting into a groove in his first season with Las Vegas, catching 14 of 28 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown over eight contests so far.

9482.short: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
9482.long: The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.

13305.short: Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
13305.long: The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.

10213.short: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
10213.long: Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

12527.short: Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
12527.long: The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.

11604.short: Bowers caught seven of eight targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for two yards and lost a fumble.
11604.long: Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.

12584.short: Porter (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 9 battle against the 49ers.
12584.long: Porter suffered a groin injury last Sunday against the Jets and logged a DNP/LP/FP practice progression this week. He was questionable to suit up entering Sunday but will ultimately be able to give it a go. Porter ranks second on the Raiders with five defensed passes on the season.

7039.short: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
7039.long: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.

4033.short: Njoku (fibula), who is still on IR, was limited in practice Friday.
4033.long: Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return -- in his lone full game of the season so far (Week 1 against Arizona), he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards.

11749.long: Hart upgraded to full participation in Friday's practice after being limited during Thursday's session. The cornerback therefore should be set to suit up for Monday night's contest against the Ravens.

8519.short: Leonard (concussion) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
8519.long: Leonard was upgraded to full participation for Friday's session after being limited Thursday. The cornerback has not yet officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, but a return to full practice means he should be all set to suit up for the Chargers' Monday night contest against the Ravens.

12509.short: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
12509.long: After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

9511.short: Mitchell (hip) remained limited at practice Friday.
9511.long: It's a new injury for Mitchell, who also was limited Thursday when the Chargers filed their first practice report for the upcoming Monday night game at Baltimore. He'll have some extra motivation, facing his former team in primetime as his current team seeks its first win of the season.

11635.long: McConkey -- who dealt with back spasms last Sunday and as a result didn't log any snaps in the 0-8 Chargers' loss to the Texans, has now missed back-to-back practices, so what he's able to do Saturday will be pivotal with regard to his status for Monday night's game against the Ravens. If McConkey is unavailable for the contest, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith would be in line to head Los Angeles' WR corps, as they did versus Houston.

13380.long: Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders. It appears he will remain on the shelf for Monday's game versus the Ravens unless he shows signs of progress in the next few days.

6797.short: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
6797.long: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

10914.short: Henley remains with the Chargers, as the Broncos have backed out of trading for the linebacker, Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com reports.
10914.long: A trade involving Henley was agreed to Tuesday pending a physical, but the Broncos apparently found a red flag concerning his knee during that physical. Denver offered an updated trade to the Chargers with different draft compensation than the originally agreed upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, but the two sides were unable to agree on an updated framework, so Henley will ultimately remain with the Chargers. Henley has not missed a game this season, so the concern Denver discovered on his physical isn't expected to impact his availability for Monday's game against the Ravens.

12670.short: Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston.
12670.long: Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

11647.short: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.
11647.long: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

12493.short: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
12493.long: Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

8127.short: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
8127.long: Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

8259.short: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
8259.long: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

12773.short: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
12773.long: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

9754.short: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
9754.long: Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

12507.short: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
12507.long: Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

10234.short: Davis caught one of two targets for a 15-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
10234.long: With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.

8364.short: McDuffie (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
8364.long: McDuffie was a DNP for both Wednesday and Thursday before logging a limited session Friday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag, but head coach Sean McVay relayed optimism Friday that McDuffie would be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt, per Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register. Emmanuel Forbes, Josh Wallace and Cam Lampkin would all be in line for larger roles in the secondary if McDuffie cannot play or operates under a snap count.

7136.short: Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Friday that he is optimistic that Curl (toe) will be available for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
7136.long: Curl opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to a toe injury before logging a limited session Friday, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. That was enough for Curl to get the questionable tag for Sunday's game, although McVay's comments suggest that the veteran safety is on the probable side to play in Week 10. If Curl cannot play or operates under a snap count, then Jaylen McCollough would be in line for a larger role in the Rams' secondary.

10214.short: Allen (oblique) is questionable for Sunday's game against Arizona, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
10214.long: Allen put together an LP-DNP-LP practice log during Week 10 prep while managing an oblique injury, which he likely picked up during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders. If he cannot play Sunday, then Max Klare would operate as the team's TE3 behind Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Allen's status may not be officially known until about 90 minutes before the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Rams announce their list of inactive players.

13270.short: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
13270.long: Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.

6865.short: Parkinson (ribs) and Tyler Higbee (illness) have been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
6865.long: Parkinson hasn't shown much hint of matching last year's TD-fueled fantasy production, but he could see more targets in the coming weeks with both Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are the favorites for WR snaps, likely leaving the RBs and TEs to handle a larger-than-usual portion of Matthew Stafford's targets. Of course, the Rams will probably want to run the ball more often while their top receiving weapons are sidelined.

3271.short: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
3271.long: With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.

12718.short: Mumpfield will take on an increased role for the Rams while Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) are unavailable, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports.
12718.long: Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell have taken most of the WR snaps alongside Nacua since Adams landed on injured reserve. It now sounds like Adams may return in a few weeks, while Nacua is out for at least a month and uncertain beyond that. There's a big opportunity ahead, but Mumpfield has been targeted on just 23 of 168 routes (13.7 percent), which is a low rate even for someone sharing the field with Nacua/Adams. Atwell has an even lower target rate (11.6 percent), so the Rams likely need their RBs and TEs to take on more offensive burden in Nacua's absence. While targets aren't assured, Mumpfield does seem like the safest bet to log a lot of WR snaps over the next few weeks.

3973.short: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Garrett (knee) will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Arizona but is expected to play, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
3973.long: Garrett made his presence felt in his return to the lineup this past Sunday at Washington, sacking Commanders QB Jayden Daniels three times, but the Rams capped his practice reps this week due to a listed knee injury. McVay's comments indicate Garrett isn't in danger of sitting out Week 10, but the pass rusher's status nonetheless will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff.

13011.short: The Rams signed Presley to the 53-man roster Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
13011.long: Los Angeles is hurting at wide receiver, so the team signed Presley to bolster depth. The 24-year-old has appeared in just one game during his NFL career since going undrafted in 2025, though he spent all of his time on special teams.

9493.short: The Rams placed Nacua (knee) on injured reserve Thursday.
9493.long: With this transaction officially in the books, Nacua will be required to miss at least the next four games due to the PCL and MCL sprains and turf-toe injury that he sustained near the end of this past Sunday's win at Washington. During the initial stage of Nacua's absence, the Rams will lean on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith at wide receiver until Davante Adams (hamstring) is ready to return from injured reserve.

8659.short: Landman recorded seven tackles (three solo), one pass breakup and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
8659.long: Much like last season, when Landman set a career high with 132 tackles across 17 starts, he's racking up the tackles through eight games in 2026. The middle linebacker is up to 66 tackles (37 solo), three forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 86 percent of the defensive snaps. Interestingly, Landman's snaps have been cut some since he returned from a concussion in Week 8. Over the last two weeks, he's played less than 70 percent of the defensive snaps after playing more than 90 percent across Weeks 1 through 6.

8330.short: Lake recorded seven tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
8330.long: Lake was credited with a forced fumble on the final play of the game, where Washington was trying to lateral the football down the field. Byron Young made the recovery for the Rams to clinch the win. For the season, Lake has recorded 63 tackles (37 solo) and has already set career highs in pass breakups (11), interceptions (three) and forced fumbles (two). He's also on pace to set a new career high in tackles.

2133.short: Head coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Adams (hamstring) returning after the Nov. 25 against the Packers "is a realistic timeline for us," Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
2133.long: In that scenario, Adams could back in action as soon as Week 12 following the Rams' bye week. Meanwhile, Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is destined to miss multiple weeks, which, for the time being leaves Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Danielsand Xavier Smith as the healthy WRs on the team's active roster.

7562.short: Atwell recorded two catches on five targets for 16 yards during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Commanders on Sunday.
7562.long: Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.

11623.short: Whittington (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday.
11623.long: This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

11168.short: The Rams signed Smith off the 49ers' practice squad Tuesday.
11168.long: Smith had been with the Rams early in the campaign before being waived Oct. 2. He subsequently signed with San Francisco's practice squad, where he had resided until Los Angeles brought him back into the fold Tuesday. Smith drew just one target (which he didn't catch) across 80 offensive snaps over his three games with the Rams in the early portion of the season, but he could immediately factor into the mix for the next several weeks, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR, Puka Nacua (knee) is slated to miss several weeks and Jordan Whittington (back) landed on injured reserve Tuesday. Smith could also be used as a returner in Whittington's absence.

12487.short: Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains optimistic Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down.
12487.long: After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

1433.short: McManus made both of his field-goal tries and both PATs in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
1433.long: McManus' field goals were good from 33 and 20 yards, and he's now made all 13 of his kicks through three games with Los Angeles. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) now out for the foreseeable future, this offense figures to struggle to score points, downgrading McManus in the fantasy kicker rankings.

13434.short: Kacmarek (quadriceps) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
13434.long: Kacmarek upgraded his practice participation in each Week 10 prep session. The tight end went from a non-participant Wednesday to a full participant by Friday's session. Kacmarek is all set to suit up as the No. 2 tight end behind Greg Dulcich for Sunday's game against the Colts.

11056.short: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
11056.long: Wayne popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quadriceps injury, which prevented him from suiting up for Friday's session. He won't be available for Sunday's contest, and it appears the Dolphins will also be without rookie third-rounder Chris Bell (knee), who is listed as doubtful. Wayne's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22.

13311.short: Bell (knee) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Colts.
13311.long: Bell was a limited practice participant Wednesday before sitting out Thursday and Friday. The injury is to his surgically repaired knee, but coach Jeff Hafley was quick to specify that the current issue isn't related to the ACL repair from last year. It sounds like Bell could be back within a week or two. For now, No. 4 receiver Kevin Coleman figures to get more playing time.

6949.short: Brooks recorded 12 tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 19-9 loss versus the Lions.
6949.long: Brooks played all 59 of the Dolphins' defensive snaps in Week 9, and he compiled a double-digit tackle total for the fourth time in his last six games. He's easily on pace for his sixth consecutive 100-tackle season going into a Week 10 matchup at Indianapolis.

13453.short: Rodriguez recorded 10 tackles (seven solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 19-9 loss versus the Lions.
13453.long: Rodriguez and the entire Dolphins defense performed well against a strong Detroit offense in Week 9, especially against the run. Rodriguez also recorded the first sack of his pro career late in the first quarter, pushing quarterback Jared Goff out of bounds for no gain. He ranks seventh in the NFL in total tackles on the season going into a Week 10 tilt at Indianapolis.

8666.short: The Dolphins designated Baker (knee) for return to practice from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
8666.long: Baker has been on Miami's PUP list since August, but it looks like he's making progress toward returning to game action soon. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which the Dolphins can activate him before they'd be required to keep him inactive for the rest of the campaign.

11643.short: Wright (quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
11643.long: After missing last Sunday's loss to the Lions, Wright figures to be back in as the lightly used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon, though Wright has not produced when on the field this season. He's averaged 1.9 yards per carry on 22 attempts and is virtually a zero in the passing game.

8161.short: The Dolphins hope Willis (abdomen) will return this year but haven't ruled out season-ending surgery, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
8161.long: With that in mind, coach Jeff Hafley noted that Willis had an MRI to assess his core muscle injury and will continue to explore medical opinions. The team already placed Willis on injured reserve, ruling him out through Week 13. The latest report suggests that it's still unclear whether Willis will miss four games, the rest of the season or something in between. Kyle McCord is taking over at QB for the Dolphins in the meantime, with Hafley on Wednesday noting of Willis' job security in general, "He'll be the starting quarterback if he returns."

13338.short: Coleman wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for 16 yards.
13338.long: Coleman logged just 11 offensive snaps, and he's settled back in as the Dolphins' fourth receiver with all three of Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell healthy ahead of him on the depth chart. Coleman, a fifth-round rookie out of Missouri has no fantasy appeal.

5297.short: The Dolphins placed Sieler (biceps) on injured reserve Tuesday.
5297.long: This move was anticipated after Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps in Sunday's Week 9 loss to the Lions. The veteran defensive tackle is scheduled for surgery and will finish his ninth NFL campaign with 24 tackles, including 2.0 sacks. Zeek Biggers, Kenneth Grant and Jordan Phillips could all take on more defensive snaps with Sieler sidelined for the rest of the season.

12494.short: McCord will step in as the Dolphins' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Indianapolis after Miami placed Malik Willis (core) on injured reserve Tuesday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
12494.long: A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.

4233.short: Gonzalez reverted to the Dolphins' practice squad Monday.
4233.long: Miami now has used the maximum three standard elevations on Gonzalez, who has converted five of seven field-goal attempts and all five point-after attempts since joining the team. The Dolphins will need to sign Gonzalez to the 53-man roster if he's going to keep handling kicking duties in future weeks.

13405.short: Allen caught a 46-yard pass in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. He rushed one time for minus-1 yard.
13405.long: Allen's catch came on a fake punt, so it was an outlier of a play. He played just six offensive snaps behind clear RB1 Ollie Gordon. Since joining Miami via waivers last month, Allen has logged 31 snaps on special teams and six on offense. He has no fantasy appeal.

8172.short: Dulcich caught two of four targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.
8172.long: Entering play Sunday, Dulcich produced 13 grabs for 166 yards over his previous three games, but he took a big step back against Detroit on a day Malik Willis didn't have any answers, as he passed for just 128 yards. Dulcich doesn't catch touchdowns and plays in a low-volume, low-scoring offense, making him more of a TE2 headed into Week 10 against the Colts.

11610.short: Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions.
11610.long: Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

13296.short: Douglas secured six of eight targets for 70 yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
13296.long: Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions, receiving yards and targets, as the rookie third-round pick continued to profile as one of Malik Willis' most reliable targets. Douglas' catch and target totals were also new career highs, while his yardage tally tied for the second highest of his nascent NFL tenure. Douglas should continue to play a key role in Miami's air attack over the second half of the season as the Dolphins look to continue cultivating their young talent.

12495.short: Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
12495.long: Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

12683.short: Ingram-Dawkins (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
12683.long: Ingram-Dawkins injured his ankle during the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday. The injury prevented him from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep, so he won't be available for Sunday's NFC North showdown. Elijah Williams and Domonique Orange are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Ingram-Dawkins, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

6901.short: Metellus (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Green Bay, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
6901.long: Metellus was a late addition to the Vikings' practice report, with the veteran safety popping up as a limited participant for Friday's session due to a shoulder injury. His late addition is concerning for the Vikings, and if Metellus cannot play Sunday, then Theo Jackson and Jay Ward would be the top candidates to start at safety alongside Harrison Smith.

6217.short: Cashman (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
6217.long: Cashman entered the league's concussion protocol following the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday. He was cleared to participate in Friday's practice in a no-contact jersey, per Goessling, but Cashman will not clear league protocol in time for Sunday's NFC North tilt. Ivan Pace will be the next man up at inside linebacker next to Eric Wilson due to the absence of Cashman, whose next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

3161.short: Wentz (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Green Bay, but Kirk Cousins will be Minnesota's starting quarterback.
3161.long: Kyler Murray (hamstring) is out for another week but may eventually replace Wentz as the No. 2 quarterback. Wentz's miserable performance against the Bills last week likely was a factor in the Vikings trading for Cousins.

7049.short: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay.
7049.long: Jennings opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNP listings due to a calf injury and now will miss his second contest of the campaign. With Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Justin Jefferson, Myles Price and Tai Felton currently are the healthy wide receivers on the Vikings' active roster.

5849.short: Murray (hamstring) was ruled out for Sunday's contest in Green Bay.
5849.long: After head coach Kevin O'Connell called Murray week-to-week due to his Grade 2 hamstring injury Wednesday, per Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com, the quarterback's second straight absence as a result was expected. O'Connell announced recent acquisition Kirk Cousins as the Vikings' starting QB for Week 10, and that should hold even after Murray gets back to full health.

1166.short: Head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday that Cousins will start Sunday's contest at Green Bay.
1166.long: Cousins was acquired from the Raiders before Tuesday's trade deadline, and after leading the first-team offense during the entirety of Week 10 prep, he'll get the nod under center in his return to Minnesota. In nine starts with Las Vegas this season, he completed 202 of 315 passes (64 percent) for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions while adding two more TDs on the ground.

9756.short: Addison is listed as questionable for Sunday's game in Green Bay due to a thumb injury.
9756.long: Addison didn't make an appearance on the Vikings' Week 10 injury report until Friday, and now his status is up in the air ahead of Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. If he's able to suit up this weekend, he'll be on the receiving end of passes from new starting QB Kirk Cousins.

5844.short: Hockenson (wrist) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay.
5844.long: Hockenson wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep due to wrist and chest injuries and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. In Hockenson's absence, Ben Yurosek and Gavin Bartholomew will step into more prominent roles in the Vikings offense, while Devin Culp will be a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad.

4413.short: Wilson recorded nine tackles (three solo) in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
4413.long: The veteran linebacker has started all eight games this season, logging 94 percent of the defensive snaps for Minnesota. He's now up to 50 tackles (24 solo), including 3.0 sacks, seven QB hits and a pass breakup. He's been extremely productive under defensive coordinator Brian Flores over the last two seasons, recording 9.5 sacks as an off-bal linebacker across 25 regular-season games during that span.

6794.short: Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Michael F. Florio of ESPN.com reports.
6794.long: Jefferson averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older than when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

12496.short: Felton went without a target while playing six of the Vikings' 48 offensive snaps in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
12496.long: Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

6931.short: Dallas caught his only target for a two-yard gain in Monday's Week 9 loss to the Bills.
6931.long: Dallas notched just eight offensive snaps but also contributed 19 snaps on special teams. The veteran running back went without a carry for the fourth time over Minnesota's past five games, indicating his lack of a role in the running game. Overall this season, Dallas has been a very small part of the Vikings' offense, recording four carries for 14 yards and five catches for 36 yards (on five targets) through eight contests.

13075.short: Price caught one of his four targets for six yards in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo on Monday Night Football. He also gained 12 yards on one punt return and brought back four kickoffs for 124 yards.
13075.long: Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

11792.short: Reichard made both of his field-goal attempts during the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday.
11792.long: After missing his lone field-goal attempt in Week 8 against the Lions, Reichard bounced back Monday to connect on field goals from 43 and 53 yards in the second quarter, which ended up being the only points that the Vikings scored. Reichard's 20 made field goals through eight regular-season games is tied for fourth-most in the NFL, and his seven makes from 50-plus yards is tied with Ka'imi Fairbairn for second behind Spencer Shrader (eight). The Vikings are 6-2 despite their struggles on offense this season, but the acquisition of Kirk Cousins should help make the unit more efficient. Minnesota will travel to Lambeau Field for Week 10 against Green Bay on Nov. 15.

12775.short: Brosmer completed six of seven attempts for 58 yards in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
12775.long: Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

4199.short: Jones rushed five times for 16 yards and brought in his only target for five yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
4199.long: Jones and backfield mate Jordan Mason combined for just 11 carries on an abysmal night for the Vikings offense, and the latter was much more efficient than Jones by averaging 5.8 yards per carry on his six totes. Jones now has seen his rushing yardage totals drop in three straight games, and Mason's return from injured reserve has played a role in the former seeing just 18 total carries in the last three contests. Jones retains a very modest outlook for a Week 10 road matchup against his old Packers teammates Sunday.

8408.short: Mason rushed six times for 35 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
8408.long: Mason was markedly more efficient than backfield mate Aaron Jones with his opportunities, averaging 5.8 yards per carry compared to the latter's 3.2. Both backs' touches were limited due to game script, however, but Mason's YPC was an encouraging figure. The veteran back next takes aim at the Packers defense in a Week 10 road matchup on Sunday.

2130.short: Van Noy (calf) has returned to Monday night's matchup with Buffalo, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
2130.long: Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

13347.short: The Vikings placed Claiborne (knee) on injured reserve Monday.
13347.long: Claiborne suffered a knee injury during a recent practice. While head coach Kevin O'Connell stated he doesn't believe Claiborne will require surgery, the injury is severe enough to keep him off the field for at least four games. The 23-year-old hasn't done much from a statistical standpoint throughout the 2026 campaign, amassing just 13 yards off six carries while garnering two catches for eight yards.

8496.short: Jackson (quadriceps) is active for Monday's game against Buffalo, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
8496.long: Jackson did not practice Thursday and Friday. While he practiced in a limited capacity Saturday, it still wasn't enough to avoid a questionable designation. However, Jackson has since been upgraded and is ready to go versus the Bills.

8726.short: Schooler (hamstring) is questionable to play against the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
8726.long: Schooler was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury he sustained during the Patriots' Week 9 loss to the Packers. He ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and his absence would deplete the Patriots' depth both in the secondary and on special teams. Starting safety Kevin Byard (chest) is also listed as questionable despite logging a full practice Friday.

12137.short: Woods (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
12137.long: Woods was unable to play against the Packers in Week 9 due to a hamstring injury. He opened Week 10 prep with consecutive limited practices before participating in full Friday, but his official status for Sunday's contest may not be known until New England announces its list of inactive players about 90 minutes before the 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. Carlton Davis (knee) did not travel with the team to Germany, and if Woods is not cleared to play Sunday, then Channing Canada and Karon Prunty would be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback.

3233.short: Following a full practice Friday, Byard (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
3233.long: Byard opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to fade the injury tag for Sunday's international game, so the veteran safety's status may not be officially known until the Patriots announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. Jaylen Reed would be the top candidate to start alongside Craig Woodson at safety if Byard is not cleared to play against Detroit.

3214.short: Henry (foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Lions after logging another limited practice Friday.
3214.long: Though Henry was limited at practice all three days leading up to the contest, the Patriots were likely managing his reps in anticipation of having the tight end available this weekend. While it's possible that the team will get top WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) back versus Detroit, RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is still out and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is banged up, so Henry figures to be a key available option for QB Drake Maye to work with, provided he avoids any setbacks with his foot.

7611.short: Stevenson (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
7611.long: Despite a report earlier in the week indicating that Stevenson would likely miss some time, the running back's ability to log limited practices both Thursday and Friday gives him a chance to play this weekend. With a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled, those considering Stevenson or A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) in Week 10 fantasy lineups will have the duo's statuses clarified before the first wave of games Sunday. Moreover, there's a pretty good chance that NFL insiders such as Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network and Adam Schefter of ESPN will provide some updates on New England's injury situation either late Saturday or early Sunday. If the team ends up holding Stevenson out ahead of a Week 11 bye, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next in line for backfield work versus Detroit this weekend, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) still sidelined.

5859.short: Brown (knee/ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
5859.long: The same applies to RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), with coach Mike Vrabel having said "pretty good" when asked before Friday's practice about his view on how the duo was progressing toward playing this weekend. Fortunately for those considering Brown (who was listed as limited at practice Wednesday through Friday) in Week 10 fantasy lineups, his status will be known before the first wave of games Sunday, with a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled.

12529.short: Coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that Henderson (illness) is working hard to get back, while acknowledging that he doesn't have a timetable for when that may occur, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
12529.long: On the topic of when the running back might return, Vrabel noted Friday, "when that is, I don't know. I don't have a timetable." Henderson, who last saw game action in Week 7, has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions, and based on Vrabel's statement, the 2025 second-rounder's status beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye is unclear. Fellow RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) returned to a limited practice Thursday, but if he ends up being held out this weekend, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the team's backfield work versus Detroit, with Terrell Jennings representing a possible practice squad elevation.

10881.short: Gonzalez logged 10 tackles (nine solo) and one pass defense during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers in Week 9.
10881.long: Gonzalez's 10 stops were a season high, but the larger concern was his poor performance in coverage. Per Pro Football Focus, Gonzalez was on coverage for 11 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and quarterback Jordan Love had a 158.3 passing rating while targeting the fourth-year defensive back. It wasn't the performance that the Patriots were expecting after signing Gonzalez to a lucrative four-year, $135 million contract extension in September. Things won't get easier for him or the Patriots' secondary, as they travel to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions, whose offense ranks fourth in the NFL in yards per game (379.8).

5054.short: Davis (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
5054.long: Davis suffered a knee injury during the Patriots' loss to the Packers this past Sunday. New England already ruled out the veteran defensive back for Week 10, so Charles Woods (hamstring), Channing Canada and Karon Prunty figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Davis will have more time to recover for Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

7204.short: Gilliam (ankle) was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
7204.long: The fullback hasn't played since Week 4. He's logged 58 snaps on offense and another 39 on special teams across four appearances this season.

12969.short: Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams.
12969.long: Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

12547.short: Williams failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
12547.long: With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

13421.short: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
13421.long: Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.

12713.short: Borregales made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
12713.long: Borregales didn't attempt a field goal, and it was the second time this season that he didn't kick any. For the year, the second-year kicker in 10 of 13 on FGAs and has made 23 of 24 extra points. He'll be a fantasy target for next Sunday's potential shootout in Detroit.

12491.short: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
12491.long: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

9501.short: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
9501.long: Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

11564.short: Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions while adding one rush for three yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
11564.long: Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.

4177.short: Hollins caught three of six targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Patriots.
4177.long: After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.

13387.short: Miller (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Carolina, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
13387.long: The rookie second-rounder was held out of practice both Thursday and Friday due to a knee injury, and his next chance to play is Week 11 against the Bears on Sunday, Nov. 22. Khristian Boyd, Colby Wooden and Tyree Wilson are all in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Miller's absence.

8390.short: Emerson (shin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
8390.long: Emerson's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a shin injury. He was able to play through the injury in Week 9 against the Browns, and he finished that contest with two solo tackles in a 23-22 overtime win for the Saints. Second-year pro Quincy Riley would likely be the next man up at outside cornerback opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry if Emerson is unable to play Sunday.

13277.short: Donaldson (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
13277.long: Donaldson will miss a third straight game, while Travis Etienne (hamstring) has a chance to return from injured reserve. With Etienne listed as questionable, Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara could have significant roles. Donaldson mostly has played in obvious passing situations this year, often staying in as a blocker.

7543.short: Etienne (hamstring) said Friday that "the week of practice went well," and that he hopes to be active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
7543.long: Etienne remains on injured reserve and officially is listed as questionable for Week 10, per Ross Jackson of WWL-TV. After the Saints designated Etienne for return from IR on Wednesday, he opened the week with back-to-back limited sessions before logging a full practice Friday, but the team still will need to activate him by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to play Sunday. With CJ Donaldson (shoulder) ruled out, Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime will be the other RBs to vie with for touches if Etienne is able to suit up this weekend.

5857.short: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.
5857.long: Fant was limited at Wednesday's practice, but the veteran TE faced no limitations Thursday, suggesting that he'll be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He has worked as the Saints' No. 2 option at the position behind Juwan Johnson.

4035.short: Kamara (rest/back) was a full practice participant Thursday.
4035.long: Kamara was listed as a non-participant Wednesday due to the combination of rest and back, but his return to all drills one day later gives him the all-clear ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Panthers. He may be welcoming back fellow RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) in Week 10 after the latter was designated for return from IR and so far has managed a pair of limited sessions, while Audric Estime is coming off a 16-touch showing this past Sunday versus the Browns.

7647.short: Werner registered 11 tackles (three solo) during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9.
7647.long: Werner co-led the Saints in tackles in Week 9, and it was the third time he's reached double-digit stops over his last four outings. Werner is on pace to record his first 100-plus tackle campaign of his six-year NFL career and is up to 65 tackles (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

5912.short: Granderson recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9.
5912.long: Granderson took down Shedeur Sanders for sacks of six and nine yards in the second and third quarters, respectively. Granderson has logged at least 1.5 sacks in each of his last four outings, and his 7.5 sacks on the year are tied for fourth-most in the NFL and one shy from matching his career high in 2023. The Saints will stay home for Week 10 against the Panthers and Bryce Young, who has been sacked 26 times, which is fourth-most in the NFL.

6302.short: Elliss recorded 11 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Saints' 23-22 overtime victory over the Browns in Week 9.
6302.long: Elliss entered Week 9 without a sack to his name, but he changed that early in the first quarter after taking down Shedeur Sanders for a seven-yard loss. Elliss' 11 stops co-led the Saints, and the veteran linebacker is up to 41 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense across five regular-season games.

13281.short: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that Tyson should get "a healthy dose more" of snaps in Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
13281.long: Tyson played just 18 snaps and lost a fumble on his first catch this past Sunday against the Browns, but there were some positives from his regular-season debut, including a strong target rate (five targets on 16 routes). While there's no assurance of a full-time role, Tyson at least figures to take more snaps away from fellow rookie Bryce Lance, if not from veteran Devaughn Vele.

13533.short: Brown caught his only target for 52 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win versus the Browns. He also lost a fumble on a punt return.
13533.long: Brown showed off his plus speed in the second quarter, blowing by safety Ronnie Hickman and coming down with a 52-yard bomb from quarterback Tyler Shough. One series later, though, he coughed up the football during an erratic punt return. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on New Orleans' depth chart, there likely won't be much room in the short term for him to earn a significant role outside of special teams.

13420.short: Lance failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
13420.long: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.

11653.short: The Saints reverted Smyth to their practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
11653.long: Smyth was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 9 overtime win over Cleveland. He served as New Orleans' kicker in the contest and went 3-for-4 on FGAs while making both of his PAT attempts. That performance was likely good enough for Smyth to be elevated again for this Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.

11834.short: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
11834.long: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

7002.short: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
7002.long: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

8396.short: McFadden made 10 tackles (five solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
8396.long: McFadden logged one tackle for loss in the contest. The starting inside linebacker assisted the Giants in holding the Commanders to 3.2 yards per carry and no rushing touchdowns in the game.

7666.short: Holland logged three tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
7666.long: Holland picked off Jayden Daniels with 2:19 left in the fourth quarter, just one Commanders drive after Ar'Darius Washington picked the quarterback off. Despite back-to-back turnovers, the Giants' offense logged back-to-back three-and-outs to put the Commanders' offense in position to win the game.

7970.short: Washington accumulated seven tackles (five solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
7970.long: Washington broke up two passes in the contest, picking off Jayden Daniels with 5:31 left in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game. Despite making a crucial play with the Giants up four points, the offense could not put more points on the board to cement a primetime win.

13377.short: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
13377.long: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

13833.short: Zvada missed his only field-goal try and made all three of his PATs on Thursday in a loss to Washington.
13833.long: Zvada's miss was a chip-shot 33-yarder in the first quarter that sailed wide left. That proved to be a critical mistake, as the Commanders won by just three points. Zvada appeared to shore up his job security a bit by going 4-for-4 on FG tries in Week 9 against Philadelphia, but it's hard to ignore the fact that he's gone just 17-for-23 on field-goal attempts overall and has missed three kicks from under 50 yards. The rookie does have a perfect 16-for-16 mark on extra-point attempts, and head coach John Harbaugh expressed support for the inconsistent kicker Friday, saying of Zvada, "I'm confident that he's going to become a good kicker. If at some point and time it doesn't happen, it doesn't happen. But I'm not going to panic halfway through the season with a guy who has made a bunch of kicks," Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.

11597.short: Johnson logged one catch (on three targets) for eight yards Thursday in a loss to the Commanders.
11597.long: Johnson hasn't been able to get going in 2026, as he's finished with one or zero catches in six of his seven games so far. After working as New York's top tight end last season, he's been mostly an afterthought in the current campaign due to the arrival of Isaiah Likely, who went off for a 9-127-1 line on a team-leading 11 targets Thursday. As long as Likely is healthy, Johnson won't have much appeal in most fantasy formats.

7090.short: Mooney caught two of five targets for eight yards Thursday in a loss to Washington.
7090.long: Mooney logged the third-most targets of any New York pass catcher, but he managed just two short receptions. Efficiency has been an issue for the veteran wideout throughout the campaign, as he's hauled in only 14 of 30 targets through nine contests. Mooney has finished with fewer than 10 yards in four of his past six appearances, so he's not a viable fantasy play at the moment.

6130.short: Singletary played just five snaps on offense and took one carry for three yards in Thursday's 24-21 loss to the Commanders.
6130.long: Cam Skattebo came back from a hamstring injury and dominated backfield work, taking 21 touches for 122 yards and two touchdowns on an 88 percent snap share. Singletary played 92 percent of snaps the week before in a win at Philadelphia, but his 23 touches went for just 39 total yards and no TDs. It'll likely be another large workload for Skattebo when the Giants host the Jaguars in Week 11.

13285.short: Fields brought in three of four targets for 62 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
13285.long: The rookie finished a distant second in receiving yards to Isaiah Likely for the Giants on the night, but Fields' yardage total was the second highest of his nascent career. Fields has at least three catches in three consecutive games after opening his career with six straight two-reception efforts, and the Notre Dame product will look to continue cultivating his chemistry with J.J. McCarthy in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

11565.short: McCarthy completed 23 of 36 passes for 293 yards with a touchdown and an interception while adding six rushes for 34 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
