11565.long: McCarthy continued to look like a competent NFL signal-caller in his third start for the Giants, posting a new career high in passing yards and adding a new season high in rushing yardage. His one touchdown pass was a critical one, as he hit Isaiah Likely over the middle for a 66-yard score just before the midway point of the fourth quarter to erase a 17-14 deficit. McCarthy has displayed excellent chemistry with his top targets, and he'll look to keep his hot streak going against a pass-funnel Jaguars defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

11632.short: Nabers secured five of seven targets for 44 yards and lost a fumble in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
11632.long: The star wideout finished with less than 50 receiving yards for the second time in five days, and Nabers' late third-quarter lost fumble had significant ramifications. The turnover came at the Commanders' 16-yard line with the Giants down by three, costing  New York a golden opportunity to tie the game at minimum. Nabers' aforementioned pair of mediocre performances have come in the wake of a four-game streak of 100-yard efforts in Weeks 4-7, and he'll look to boost his numbers back up against the Jaguars' pass-funnel defense in a Week 11 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 22.

8131.short: Likely brought in nine of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown and fumbled once but recovered in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
8131.long: Likely set the pace for the Giants across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his figure in the middle category also was a career high. The veteran tight end now has five double-digit target tallies on the campaign, and Thursday's production, which included a 66-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the third quarter, pushed his season line to a robust 55-575-7 line across nine games. All three components already are career-high figures, affording Likely massive momentum heading into a Week 11 home showdown against the Jaguars on Sunday, Nov. 22.

12481.short: Skattebo rushed 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and brought in three of four targets for 44 yards in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
12481.long: Skattebo put together an impressive all-around performance that included a season high in receiving yards. He also exceeded the 75-yard mark on the ground for the third time on the campaign, and he went in for his third and fourth rushing touchdowns of the season on one- and 13-yard runs in the first and third quarters, respectively. Skattebo didn't show any ill effects from the hamstring injury that cost him Sunday's win over the Eagles, and he'll now gear up for a Week 11 home matchup against the Jaguars' elite run defense on Sunday, Nov. 22.

7816.short: Pinnock (back) is questionable to return to Thursday night's contest against the Commanders, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
7816.long: Pinnock exited the game early in the third quarter with a back injury, and his status for the rest of the game is uncertain. In his absence, Tyler Nubin will be thrust into a more prominent role in New York's secondary.

6867.short: Harrison (groin) is inactive for Thursday's game against Washington, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
6867.long: Harrison was limited at practice throughout the week and has since been ruled out for the Week 10 meeting with the Commanders. The 28-year-old has played sparingly on defense during the 2026 campaign, though his absence will be felt on special teams. Harrison's next opportunity to suit up will come in Week 11 versus Jacksonville.

12574.short: Carter (knee/back) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Commanders.
12574.long: Carter logged limited practices Monday and Tuesday before upgrading to full practice Wednesday. Across eight starts this season, the No. 3 overall pick of the 2025 Draft has produced 19 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble. He has yet to develop into a game-wrecking edge rusher.

13367.short: Head coach John Harbaugh told reporters that Hood dislocated his finger during Tuesday's practice, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
13367.long: Hood left Tuesday's practice with a trainer after injuring his finger, but Harbaugh told reporters after the session that the rookie second-rounder will "be fine." It's possible that Hood doesn't miss any game time, although Wednesday's injury report will shed light on his status for Thursday's NFC East tilt against the Commanders. Most of his playing time has been on special teams, but Hood's absence would give the Giants less depth in the secondary.

7687.short: Wright (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against Buffalo.
7687.long: A back injury prevented Wright from playing against the Chiefs in Week 9. He logged a full practice Friday, but it wasn't enough for him to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's AFC East tilt. His absence would mean less depth in the Jets' secondary and one less contributor on special teams.

5049.short: Phillips (ankle) is questionable against the Bills on Sunday.
5049.long: Phillips missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep while recovering from an ankle injury. He was a full participant in Friday's session, so he may be considered more toward the probable side of playing Sunday. If Phillips cannot play, then both Jack Heflin and Payton Page would be in line for more rotational snaps on the interior defensive line behind Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson.

7678.short: Ossai (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills.
7678.long: Ossai has a chance to return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury after stringing together a trio of limited practices during Week 10 prep. His return would give the Jets additional depth at defensive end behind Kingsley Enagbare and David Bailey.

11766.short: Brownlee (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Buffalo.
11766.long: Brownlee was unable to practice Thursday due to an illness, but he was back on the field Friday in a limited capacity. He'll have the weekend to shake off his illness, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Jets announce their list of inactive players. Rookie second-rounder D'Angelo Ponds would have a larger role in the Jets' secondary if Brownlee is not cleared to play.

11724.short: Wallace (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
11724.long: Wallace was held out of practice all week while recovering from a groin injury, which will prevent him from playing in a second consecutive game. Most of his snaps this season have come on special teams, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at linebacker for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Wallace's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

13276.short: Cooper (ankle), who was a full participant in Friday's practice, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills.
13276.long: The same goes for top receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) as well as Adonai Mitchell (knee). The trio's full practice participation Friday suggests that all three players will be available Sunday, but their statuses will nonetheless need to be confirmed ahead of Week 10 action due to their official game designations. Fortunately for fantasy managers who have shares in any of the Jets' top three WRs, the team kicks off at 1:00 pm ET on Sunday.

11625.short: Mitchell (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills after he was a full participant in Friday's practice.
11625.long: Fellow wideouts Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Omar Cooper (ankle) also are listed as questionable despite being full practice participants Friday. Both figure to play, as does Mitchell, who finished without a catch on seven targets (two drops) in last week's loss to the Chiefs -- one week after catching seven passes for 142 yards and a TD against the Raiders. Wilson's likely return to the lineup means Mitchell isn't assured of similar volume moving forward.

8146.short: Wilson (concussion) has one more step to complete in concussion protocol, and Jets coach Aaron Glenn believes that will happen before Sunday's game against the Bills, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
8146.long: Wilson will upgrade to full participation Friday after logging limited practices earlier in the week. He's on track to return after missing just one game, but he'll still need clearance from a neurologist if Friday's practice goes as planned.

13363.short: Bailey tallied nine tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two forced fumbles during the Jets' loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
13363.long: Bailey had a productive outing despite the loss as he was the only Jets defender to record a sack. The 23-year-old has gotten off to a strong start during his rookie campaign, compiling 34 tackles (26 solo), including 7.5 sacks, and five forced fumbles across his first eight games.

11608.short: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.
11608.long: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

12498.short: Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
12498.long: Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

11571.short: Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
11571.long: With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.

6353.short: The Jets signed Reeder to their active roster Monday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
6353.long: Reeder is returning to New York after having been released by the Jets in October. The 32-year-old has logged four tackles (one solo) across six outings this season and will likely continue to see the majority of his playing time come on special teams during his second tenure with the Jets.

10883.short: McDonald put in a request for the Jets to trade him ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Ian Rapoport and Rich Cimini of ESPN report.
10883.long: The 2023 first-round pick racked up 18.5 sacks over the previous two seasons and has three on his ledger through nine games in 2026, but he's seen his playing time tail off with the arrival of No. 2 overall pick David Bailey and the addition of Kingsley Enagbare in free agency. Though McDonald is hopeful to land with a team that can present him with a clearer path to a full-time role, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Monday that McDonald "is going to be here" once the deadline passes, per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic.

5119.short: Sanders went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
5119.long: Sanders provided all the offense for New York in Week 9, making exactly four field goals for the second straight week and third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards before pulling his lone miss wide left from 53 yards, all of which came in the first half. Sanders has now gone 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

13330.short: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
13330.long: After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

1373.short: Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed once for eight yards.
1373.long: Smith struggled in the absence of top wide receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion), as the Jets made four field goals in the first half before getting blanked in the second half. The veteran QB posted his second-lowest total of the season for passing yards and was held without a touchdown for the first time since Week 1. Smith could be busy in Week 10 with the 2-7 Jets likely to be forced into a pass-heavy game plan if they fall behind against the Bills.

11576.short: Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
11576.long: Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.

8155.short: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
8155.long: Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.

13567.short: Payne (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 clash against Kansas City.
13567.long: Payne has been on IR all season but was designated to return Wednesday. Despite being a full participant in practice all week, he isn't quite ready for game action. Payne's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.

8395.short: Belton recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo) and a pass defensed in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
8395.long: Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.

7841.short: Sherwood recorded 14 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
7841.long: Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.

11752.short: Trotter recorded 11 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants in Week 9.
11752.long: Trotter was on the field for 64 of the Eagles' 67 defensive snaps (95.5 percent), and he was the only Philadelphia defender to reach double-digit stops. He's tallied at least 10 tackles three times in 2026, and the third-year pro is up to 51 tackles (32 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

7596.short: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-3 yards during the Eagles' 19-11 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
7596.long: Week 9 was the Eagles' first game with Joe Milton as the starter, with Tanner McKee relegated to backup duties. Milton completed 18 of his 34 passes, and his lone connection with Moore resulted in a three-yard loss. The Eagles are on a bye for Week 10, and Moore's role on the offense would evaporate if one or both of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was cleared to play in Week 11 against the Steelers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

13150.short: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
13150.long: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

8325.short: Ebiketie will remain with the Eagles after his reported trade to the Bengals on Tuesday fell through and won't be completed, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
8325.long: Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.

7561.short: Mitchell reverted to the Eagles' practice squad Monday.
7561.long: Mitchell has been elevated each of the past three weeks and has logged at least six touches in every game during that span. During this past Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants, he recorded six yards on three carries and caught three passes for 20 yards on four targets. The Eagles would need to sign Mitchell to the 53-man roster in order for him to be eligible to play in their next game, which will be Nov. 22 versus Pittsburgh following a Week 10 bye. That opportunity for Mitchell could depend on whether Tank Bigsby (abdomen) and/or Will Shipley (foot) return from injured reserve.

4195.short: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
4195.long: Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.

13349.short: Stowers failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
13349.long: The rookie tight end ran just four routes on Joe Milton's 48 dropbacks against the G-Men. Grant Calcaterra ran just six, as the Eagles used more three-wide sets than multiple TE sets. Stowers would need a Dallas Goedert injury or trade to come into any fantasy value.

13294.short: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
13294.long: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

5022.short: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
5022.long: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

11557.short: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
11557.long: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

4866.short: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
4866.long: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

6815.short: Baun (back) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Giants.
6815.long: Baun exited the second half of Sunday's game with a back injury. Smael Mondon will fill in at inside linebacker opposite Jeremiah Trotter while Baun receives further medical evaluation to determine if he can return to the contest.

9230.short: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
9230.long: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

10873.short: Smith (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Commanders.
10873.long: Smith was a full participant in Friday's practice, and he was cleared from the league's concussion protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Jalyx Hunt, Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa.

12561.short: Harmon (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
12561.long: Harmon missed the Steelers' four games prior to the Week 9 bye while on injured reserve due to a foot injury. He was cleared to return to practice Wednesday and ended Week 10 prep with a full session Friday, but he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's AFC North showdown. Harmon's return would bolster the Steelers' defensive line behind Yahya Black, Keeanu Benton and Cameron Heyward.

5071.short: Elliott was a full participant in practice Thursday, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
5071.long: Elliott had no injury designation in practice Thursday after popping up as a limited participant in practice Wednesday. The 29-year-old has played just two games through nine weeks of the NFL regular season. He returned from injured reserve in Week 7, totaling two tackles (two solo) on the season.

6819.short: Pittman (foot) is warmed up with his teammates Thursday, though he remains on IR and wasn't wearing a helmet, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
6819.long: Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

7796.short: Echols (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
7796.long: Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.

12899.short: Slaughter (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
12899.long: Slaughter was unable to play against the Browns in Week 8 due to a hamstring injury that prevented him from practicing. His ability to log a full session Wednesday puts him on track to play against the Bengals on Sunday, when he's expected to play mostly on special teams while providing the Steelers depth in the secondary.

7757.short: Skowronek (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
7757.long: Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

1945.short: Boswell made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
1945.long: Boswell missed a 57-yard attempt on the Steelers' first offensive drive of the game. The kicker proceeded to nail 20-yard and 37-yard attempts en route to five straight made kicks. Boswell is now 18-for-23 on field-goal attempts and 16-for-16 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

13274.short: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
13274.long: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

7600.short: Freiermuth caught both of his targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns. He added one rushing attempt for a one-yard touchdown.
7600.long: With time expiring in the second quarter, Freiermuth took a direct snap and punched in a one-yard rushing score to put the Steelers up 20-6 headed into halftime. The tight end entered the season with zero career carries but now has four through eight games, turning them into five yards and a touchdown. As a receiver, Freiermuth has been held to exactly two catches in each of the last three games and has yet to hit 50 yards in any game this season. He's a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet with the Steelers headed into their bye week.

9479.short: Washington caught three of five targets for 94 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win over the Browns.
9479.long: Washington led the team in receiving yards while finishing tied for second on the team in targets with wide receiver Germie Bernard. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he reeled in a short pass from Aaron Rodgers and took off for a 58-yard gain. Washington has corralled 19 of 28 targets for 254 yards and three touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

7021.short: Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
7021.long: Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

5846.short: Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
5846.long: Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

96.short: Rodgers completed 13 of 25 passes for 172 yards with no touchdowns and one interception in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
96.long: Jaylen Warren spearheaded the Steelers' attack with 143 rushing yards and a touchdown, and backfield mate Rico Dowdle added 56 yards and a score of his own. When combined with a highly effective effort by Pittsburgh's defense, there wasn't much production required of Rodgers and the air attack after much busier games leading into Sunday. Rodgers finished with season-low figures in completions, pass attempts, completion percentage and passing yards while failing to throw a touchdown pass for the first time since Week 2, but he's highly likely to revert to his prior pass-heavy ways in a Week 10 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday night, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

8228.short: Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
8228.long: Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

7865.short: The Steelers signed Smith off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
7865.long: Smith had already been elevated from the practice squad thrice, so Saturday's move means he's eligible to suit up for the Steelers for the rest of the season. The Iowa product caught both of his targets for 24 yards against the Saints in Week 7. If Ben Skowronek (calf) cannot play Sunday, then Smith, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Johnson would all be in line for more offensive snaps.

11727.short: Wilson totaled six tackles (three solo) and an interception during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
11727.long: Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

6807.short: Queen compiled 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
6807.long: Queen had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles in addition to registering his first sack of the campaign. The 2020 first-round pick has now logged 48 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across seven games this season.

4972.short: Rudolph is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
4972.long: Rudolph has emerged as the Steelers' preferred backup quarterback behind starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers coming out of the preseason. Through each of Pittsburgh's first seven contests, Rudolph has suited up, while both Will Howard and Drew Allar have been inactive. Howard is the Steelers' emergency No. 3 quarterback and will be called upon to play only in the event that both Rodgers and Rudolph are forced to exit Sunday's game.

4070.short: Watt (calf) practiced fully Friday and doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Saints.
4070.long: Watt was limited by a calf injury Thursday, but he's good to go for Pittsburgh's Paris game against New Orleans. Through six games this season, the 32-year-old Watt has 15 tackles (10 solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery and a pick-six interception.

11697.short: Green (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Dallas.
11697.long: Green missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep due to a back injury that he sustained during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9. He was limited in Friday's practice, and if he cannot play Sunday, then rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock and Nate Hobbs (groin, IR) would be candidates for elevated roles in the secondary.

7819.short: Lenoir (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
7819.long: Lenoir injured his foot during the 49ers' Week 9 win over the Raiders. He was able to log a limited practice Friday after being sidelined both Wednesday and Thursday, and that limited session was enough for him to draw the questionable tag. Rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock and Ashtyn Davis would be in line for more snaps in the secondary if Lenoir is unable to play Sunday.

6056.short: Greenlaw (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
6056.long: Greenlaw tweaked his knee during Thursday's practice, but he was cleared to participate in Friday's session in a limited capacity, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com. Garret Wallow, Tatum Bethune and Luke Gifford would all be in line to start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger if Greenlaw is unable to play Sunday.

5872.short: Samuel (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
5872.long: Samuel was back on the practice field this week for the first time since injuring his right hamstring in Week 5 at Seattle, turning in limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. It was enough to get the clear to return to action this weekend. With Mike Evans (Achilles) out again, Samuel likely will be among the top WRs at the disposal of QB Brock Purdy along with newcomer Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins.

2216.short: Evans (Achilles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
2216.long: Evans thus will miss his third game in a row due to the right Achilles injury that he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning to action and likely would play this weekend if it was a playoff matchup. Instead, the 49ers will continue to exercise caution with their No. 1 WR. With Evans again sidelined Sunday, Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing represent the options at the position available to QB Brock Purdy.

1479.short: Allen will play for the 49ers in Sunday's game at Dallas after being acquired in a trade earlier this week, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
1479.long: Allen could have a significant role immediately, joining an injury-riddled WR room, though Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been cleared to play this Sunday. Mike Evans (Achilles) is out again, leaving Samuel, Allen, Demarcus Robinson and Jordan Watkins as the top healthy options at wide receiver. San Francisco coach Kyle Shanahan mentioned Wednesday that Allen still has some risk of being suspended at some point this season due to an August arrest for DUI while he was with the Colts, per 95.7 The Game.

13520.short: Dugger recorded six solo tackles and a pick-six during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.
13520.long: Dugger set the tone for the 49ers right out of halftime, when he intercepted a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tre Tucker and returned it 35 yards for a pick-six for the first defensive touchdown of Dugger's young NFL career. The rookie fifth-rounder has logged at least six solo tackles in three of his last four games and is up to 36 tackles (25 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pick-six through eight regular-season games.

5041.short: Warner logged five tackles (three solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.
5041.long: Warner's five stops tied a season low, although he did recover the fumble late in the third quarter that the 49ers' offense converted into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Jordan Watkins seven plays later. Warner has played every single defensive snap in each of the 49ers' last six games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 77 tackles (36 solo), including 0.5 sacks, three pass defenses, five forced fumbles and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.

12649.short: West (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
12649.long: The 49ers opened West's 21-day practice window Wednesday, and he was limited in his return to on-field practice. He landed on injured reserve in late September due to a knee injury, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Cowboys.

13501.short: The 49ers placed Halton (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday.
13501.long: Halton suffered a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over Las Vegas and is out for the season. The fourth-round rookie finished his inaugural NFL campaign with 15 tackles, including 2.0 sacks, a defensed pass, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery (which he returned for a touchdown) over eight contests. San Francisco's recent acquisition of DeForest Buckner softens the blow of losing Halton a bit.

2197.short: Cooks brought in both of his targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
2197.long: Cooks and other 49ers wide receivers operated in elevated roles Sunday due to the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cooks' 25 receiving yards ended up being third-most on the Niners behind Jordan Watkins (86) and tight end George Kittle (58), and Cooks' 32 offensive snaps were also third-most among San Francisco wide receivers. The 49ers hit the road for Week 10 against the Cowboys, and Cooks' workload on offense figures to decrease with Keenan Allen now in the fold, and with Evans or Samuel potentially ready to return.

3286.short: Robinson caught three passes for 22 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
3286.long: Playing in his first game since Week 2 due to a high ankle sprain, Robinson played 51 percent of the Niners' offensive snaps against Las Vegas. San Francisco's wideout situation is a week-to-week thing moving forward, with the Tuesday addition of Keenan Allen and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Mike Evans (Achilles) and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) all likely to return at some point in the near future. Robinson isn't someone to roster in 12-team fantasy leagues.

7527.short: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries for Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
7527.long: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.

12467.short: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas.
12467.long: As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

5189.short: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and all five of his extra-point tries during San Francisco's win over the Raiders on Sunday.
5189.long: Pineiro continues to see the majority of his action handling extra-point duties, as he's now attempted just two field goals across his last three outings and only 10 total on the season. Sunday's performance also marked just the second time this season that the 31-year-old didn't miss a kick.

6803.short: The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk (personal) from the reserve/left squad list Monday and were granted a two-week roster exemption for the wide receiver, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
6803.long: In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tearing the ACL and MCL in his right knee Oct. 20, 2024 and undergoing surgery.

13414.short: Black rushed 11 times for 70 yards but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
13414.long: Black led the 49ers in rushing yards, finishing with two more than Christian McCaffrey, but McCaffrey operated as the clear lead back and scored twice on 20 touches. McCaffrey won't be unseated as the starter while healthy, but Black has started to earn a larger role, with double-digit carries for at least 63 rushing yards in consecutive games. The rookie third-round pick is averaging a solid 4.5 yards per carry heading into a Week 10 road game against the Cowboys.

12634.short: Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
12634.long: Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.

11396.short: Pili (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
11396.long: Pili missed the Seahawks' last two games while nursing a back injury, but he's been cleared to play in Week 10 after logging a full practice session Friday. His return gives the Seahawks more depth on the interior defensive line behind Byron Murphy.

5061.short: Nwosu (ankle) does not have an injury designation against the Raiders on Sunday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
5061.long: Nwosu has missed the Seahawks' last two games while tending to an ankle injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after ending Week 10 prep with a full practice Friday. His return means less defensive snaps will be available for Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and Connor O'Toole.

10911.short: Hall (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
10911.long: Hall was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 10 prep before sitting out Friday's session. However, his reduced practice reps appear to have been planned by the Seahawks to manage his back injury, and the fourth-year pro has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. Hall has 24 tackles (14 solo), including 3.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

2311.short: Williams (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
2311.long: Williams will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a shoulder injury, which prevented him from practicing in any capacity during Week 10 prep. Mike Morris and Rylie Mills will operate in expanded roles on defense in the absence of Williams, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29, since the Seahawks are on a bye for Week 11.

5854.short: Lock (right elbow/oblique) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Brady Henderson of ESPN reports.
5854.long: Lock was listed as limited on the Seahawks' first two Week 10 injury reports due to a lingering right elbow issue and a new oblique concern. He spoke of the latter injury Thursday, telling Curtis Crabtree of Fox 13 Seattle that he's "feeling good," and Lock's ability to avoid a designation confirms as much ahead of Sunday's matchup. In three appearances (two starts) this season, Lock has completed 54 of 76 passes (71 percent) for 597 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions.

7672.short: Jones tallied seven tackles (three solo) during Seattle's win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
7672.long: Jones finished tied for second on the team in tackles behind Julian Love during Sunday's victory. Jones has now racked up seven or more tackles in all nine of his outings to start the season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Raiders.

8676.short: Shaheed (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
8676.long: Shaheed suffered a knee injury during a Week 7 win against the Chiefs and missed the last two games as a result. Now that he's unhindered on the practice field, though, he'll resume his standing as Seattle's No. 2 WR and primary kick and punt returner

11435.short: Wilson didn't log any snaps during Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
11435.long: Wilson averaged 18.2 carries for 66.7 yards over six games between Week 2 and Week 7, culminating with a 24-100-1 rushing line against Kansas City. However, that opportunity came while Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet were on IR. Both running backs returned ahead of the Week 8 matchup against Chicago, and Wilson hasn't played a single offensive snap in two games since. As long as Charbonnet and Price are both healthy, it appears Wilson is going to be relegated primarily to a special-teams role, if he plays at all.

4039.short: Kupp caught three of four targets for 32 yards during the Seahawks' 17-3 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
4039.long: All three of Kupp's catches came on the same offensive drive midway through the third quarter, which ended with a 45-yard field goal by Jason Myers. The Seahawks had Drew Lock under center due to the absence of Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs), but Lock is now dealing with an oblique injury that could prevent him from playing in Week 10 against the Raiders on Nov. 15. Jalen Milroe would be the next man up at quarterback for Seattle, which would lower the floors for Kupp and the rest of the Seahawks' pass catchers. Kupp has a 22-238-2 receiving line on 34 targets through nine regular-season games.

12048.short: Holani didn't log any touches or targets Sunday in a 17-3 win over Arizona.
12048.long: Holani logged just two offensive snaps, by far his lowest count in a game of the season. He's trending toward playing primarily on special teams now that Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price are back in the fold at running back for Seattle. Emanuel Wilson also is on the roster, but he didn't see any action at all in Week 10.

12497.short: Horton caught two passes for 22 yards on three targets in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals.
12497.long: Horton has just seven catches for 67 yards across six games since Week 3. The Seahawks' No. 3 receiver is well off the fantasy radar, even with Rashid Shaheed (knee) injured.

2747.short: Myers made his only field-goal attempt and converted both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
2747.long: The Seahawks' offense put forth a relatively modest showing in Week 9 with backup quarterback Drew Lock (oblique) at the helm, but Myers made good on the few opportunities that he did have, rebounding somewhat from a rough game in Week 8 where he missed two kicks. Starting quarterback Sam Darnold (quadriceps) will again be out in Week 10 at Las Vegas, but Myers will at least have the benefit of kicking indoors come Sunday.

4943.short: Darnold (quadriceps), who won't play this coming Sunday at Las Vegas, is expected to return in Week 12 at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 after a Week 11 bye, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
4943.long: Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

13286.short: Price posted nine carries for 24 yards and secured all four targets for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 victory versus the Cardinals.
13286.long: Price received one more touch than Week 8's 12 but more than doubled his yards from scrimmage from 37 to 78. Having said that, backfield mate Zach Charbonnet went from nine touches last Monday against the Bears to 17 in Week 9 while pacing the Seahawks in total yards with 86. Price and Charbonnet appear poised to split the RB reps moving forward, but the former may be the change-of-pace option while the latter handles early downs.

9753.short: Charbonnet took 16 carries for 77 yards and tallied one catch (on two targets) for nine yards during Sunday's 17-3 win versus the Cardinals.
9753.long: The script in the Seahawks backfield flipped from Week 8 to this Sunday, as Charbonnet nearly doubled his touch count (nine vs. 17) while Jadarian Price maintained it (12 vs. 13). Charbonnet also was far more effective with his workload, going from 29 yards from scrimmage to 86. This marked only his second outing since tearing his left ACL back in January, so he figures to keep improving his efficiency while seemingly taking on a greater share of the RB reps over Price.

11603.short: Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown.
11603.long: Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

9488.short: Smith-Njigba reeled in seven of 10 targets for 51 yards during Sunday's 17-3 win against the Cardinals.
9488.long: Smith-Njigba was working with backup QB Drew Lock for the third time this season, as the latter was filling in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/rib). The result was a season low in receiving yards, which was only the second time this season in which Smith-Njigba failed to reach the century mark. Despite the subpar outing for him, he surpassed 1,000 yards on the campaign for a third straight season, with eight games still to go. Darnold may also be sidelined next Sunday at Las Vegas, which again could impact Smith-Njigba's chances to produce as he has most weeks in 2026.

12510.short: Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports.
12510.long: Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.

11734.short: Knight (hip) doesn't have an injury designation for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
11734.long: Knight opened Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices before logging a full session Saturday, and he's done enough to fade an injury tag against Chicago. The third-year linebacker has seen an uptick in defensive snaps over his last two outings, and he's logged 16 tackles (nine solo) in that span.

11705.short: Smith recorded seven tackles (four solo) and an interception in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
11705.long: As a team, the Bucs picked off Caleb Williams four times Sunday night, but it still wasn't enough to propel Tampa Bay to a win. Smith now has two picks over his last three games and is up to 50 tackles (26 solo), three pass breakups and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. He has a chance to best last season's career-high 100 tackles in 2026.

8384.short: McCollum recorded five tackles (four solo) and two interceptions in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
8384.long: The cornerback has been on an absolute heater in the interceptions department, as he's now recorded at least one pick in three straight games. After picking off Bryce Young and Michael Penix in back-to-back games, McCollum got Caleb Williams twice in Week 9. The four interceptions are a new career high for the fifth-year defensive back, who is now up to 35 tackles (28 solo), 11 pass breakups and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.

4118.short: Anzalone posted two solo tackles and an interception during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.
4118.long: The Buccaneers picked off Caleb Williams four times, which included Anzalone's pick late in the third quarter that set up Tampa Bay in Chicago territory. Anzalone recorded four interceptions over his first nine NFL seasons, but he's already up to four picks in 2026, three of which have come over his last two outings. He enters the Week 10 bye with 44 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, through nine regular-season games.

13379.short: Trotter recorded eight tackles (five solo) during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears in Week 9.
13379.long: Trotter led the Buccaneers in tackles in Week 9, when he played 59 of 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent). The rookie second-rounder has logged at least six stops in each of the first eight games of the regular season, and he enters the Week 10 bye with 76 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass defenses (including a pick-six).

11994.short: Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
11994.long: Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

13317.short: Hurst failed to haul in his lone target during the Buccaneers' 27-24 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
13317.long: For a third consecutive game, the rookie third-rounder didn't record a catch while seeing only one target. Of more concern was the fact that Hurst was on the field for only one offensive snap in Week 9 after logging at least 25 offensive snaps in each of the first eight games of the regular season. That lack of offensive playing time coincided with the return of Emeka Egbuka, although Hurst also saw less snaps than Chris Godwin (62), Tez Johnson (52) and even David Sills (six), although Sills was cut by the Buccaneers on Tuesday. With the Buccaneers on a bye for Week 10, Hurst will look for better results in Week 11 against the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 22.

12485.short: Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
12485.long: Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

9506.short: Tucker didn't log any offensive snaps in a loss to the Bears on Sunday. He returned four kickoffs for 92 yards.
9506.long: It was the second straight week in which Tucker went without an offensive snap. That's happened despite Tampa Bay going to the ground plenty during that span. Perhaps not coincidentally, Tucker has begun working as a kick returner during the two-game stretch. It appears he's not going to get many opportunities on offense as long as Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell are healthy.

6650.short: McLaughlin converted all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his extra-point tries during Tampa Bay's loss to the Bears on Sunday.
6650.long: McLaughlin had a solid outing despite the loss, although all three of his field goals came from within 35 yards. Across his first nine outings of the season, the 30-year-old has yet to miss a kick, converting on all 22 field-goal attempts and all 18 extra-point tries.

8111.short: Otton caught four of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
8111.long: The tight end saw a team-high eight targets, drawing a 26.7 percent target share from Baker Mayfield. It still didn't translate into much in the box score, as Otton remains without a touchdown through nine games. He's turned 38 targets into 23 catches for 211 yards this season and is a low-floor fantasy option most weeks.

11584.short: Head coach Todd Bowles said Monday that the Buccaneers "will try and lessen the load" on Irving following their Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
11584.long: Though he hasn't shown any signs of wearing down while he's averaged a healthy 4.9 yards per tote through the Buccaneers' first nine games, Irving has already amassed 167 carries -- fourth-most in the NFL -- and would be on pace for a career-high 315 over the course of a 17-game schedule. Given the success they've found on the ground in recent weeks, the Buccaneers could continue to embrace a run-first attack, but expect Irving to cede a bit more work to backups Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker as Tampa Bay aims to keep their top back healthy for the long haul.

11618.short: Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
11618.long: While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

4037.short: Godwin caught two of three targets for 16 yards and added a 12-yard rush during Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
4037.long: Godwin has now gone back-to-back weeks without reeling in at least three passes after having done so in each of Tampa Bay's first seven contests this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 50 receiving yards or reach the end zone over nine games so far during the 2026 campaign, and he will remain an unappealing fantasy option when the Buccaneers return to action in Week 11 against the Lions.

7567.short: Gainwell rushed five times for 16 yards and caught all three of his targets for 60 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
7567.long: Most of Gainwell's 76 scrimmage yards came on a 44-yard catch. He has 304 scrimmage yards over the past three games after recording just 122 scrimmage yards across his first six outings for the Buccaneers. Bucky Irving rushed for two touchdowns Sunday and remains the top option in Tampa Bay's backfield, but Gainwell has started to make the most of his change-of-pace role in the Buccaneers' run-heavy offense. Gainwell will try to pick up where he left off in Week 11 against the Lions after a Week 10 bye.

4892.short: Mayfield completed 18 of 32 passes for 243 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears. He also rushed once for no gain and ran in a two-point conversion.
4892.long: Mayfield notched a season high in passing yards after finishing Tampa Bay's previous game without a completed pass, but he also threw multiple interceptions for the first time in six starts this season. He put forth a gutsy performance, getting back up from several big hits and scoring the game-tying two-point conversion with his legs to cap Tampa Bay's final drive, only for Chicago to kick a game-winning field goal on the ensuing possession. The struggling QB has taken a back seat to the Buccaneers' Bucky Irving-led running game in recent weeks, and Mayfield has an ugly 3:4 TD:INT heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye. After the bye, Mayfield will have a chance to pick up the pace in Week 11 against Detroit's vulnerable secondary.

12514.short: Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears.
12514.long: Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

6888.short: Winfield (ankle) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday night's contest against the Bears.
6888.long: Winfield sustained an ankle injury late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. With Winfield unavailable, Ifeatu Melifonwu will continue to operate as one of Tampa Bay's primary safeties versus Chicago.

12605.short: Parrish registered seven total tackles (four solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta.
12605.long: Parrish was able to notch multiple passes defensed for the fifth straight game, and he was able to reel in his second interception of the year, jumping in front of a short pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 36 total tackles (30 solo) and 13 passes defensed, including two interceptions, over seven contests so far during the 2026 regular season.

13308.short: Sharp went without a target while playing 19 of the Buccaneers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 16-0 win over the Falcons.
13308.long: After logging single-digit snaps on offense in each of the first six games of the season, Sharp appears to have firmly supplanted Ko Kieft as the Buccaneers' No. 3 tight end behind Cade Otton and Payne Durham. Sharp played a quarter of the snaps in a Week 7 win over the Buccaneers before bumping up to a season-high 32 percent share during Sunday's victory. The rookie sixth-round pick out of LSU will likely continue to be utilized mainly as a blocker; he's drawn just one target (a 21-yard reception) while running only nine total routes so far this season.

6065.short: Barton (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
6065.long: Barton was unable to practice during Week 10 prep while in the league's concussion protocol, which he may have entered following the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. Rookie second-rounder Anthony Hill (neck) has also been ruled out, which leaves Dorian Mausi and Mohamoud Diabate as the likely candidates to start at linebacker alongside Cedric Gray for Sunday's contest. Barton's next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22, although he would have to return to practice in at least a limited capacity to demonstrate that he's progressing in the league's five-step protocol.

13365.short: Hill (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
13365.long: Hill may have injured his neck during the Titans' Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals. The Week 9 bye provided the rookie second-rounder extra time to rest, but he was not cleared to practice during Week 10 prep and will miss his first game of the regular season. Cody Barton (concussion) has also been ruled out, so Mohamoud Diabate and Dorian Mausi both figure to start alongside Cedric Gray at linebacker for Sunday's AFC South tilt. Hill's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Nov. 22.

12540.short: Dike may have a significant role on offense with Carnell Tate (shoulder) ruled out for Sunday's game against Jacksonville.
12540.long: Tate also missed the previous game, before a Week 9 bye, when Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 43-36 overtime loss to Cincinnati. Dike played 83 percent of snaps in the contest, running more routes (33) than both Elic Ayomanor (30) and Calvin Ridley (22). The 70-percent route share was easily a season high for Dike, and his performance suggests a sizable role should be coming again this Sunday.

5967.short: Pollard (finger/rest) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
5967.long: Pollard sat out Thursday's session with a listed combo of 'finger/rest,' but given that he worked fully Friday, it was likely more of a maintenance day for Tennessee's clear-cut top back. In that role, Pollard has made his mark from a fantasy perspective by averaging 16.6 carries for 74.4 yards, with 14 catches for 70 yards and six rushing scores in eight games to date.

9508.short: Spears (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jaguars after upgrading to full practice participation Friday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
9508.long: A return to action after missing two games would hurt Tony Pollard's workload projection, though Pollard would still be in line for most of the carries. There have also been hints of rookie Nicholas Singleton getting playing time in the second half of the season, leaving Spears without much of a path to mainstream fantasy value.

13279.short: Tate (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
13279.long: There was previously some optimism that Tate -- who last played in Week 7 -- would be able to return after the Titans' Week 9 bye, but the wideout's absence will continue at least until Nov. 22 against the Cowboys, a contest that coach Robert Saleh is hopeful the No. 4 overall pick in the NFL draft will be back for, per Turron Davenport of ESPN.com. For now, added WR snaps/targets will be available for Chimere Dike and Elic Ayomanor alongside Wan'Dale Robinson, with Calvin Ridley also mixing in, an arrangement that was in play during Tennessee's Nov. 1 loss to the Bengals.

11052.short: Jones (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
11052.long: Jones was unable to play in the Titans' Week 8 loss to the Bengals due to a knee injury. He had extra time to recover courtesy of the Week 9 bye, and the fourth-year defensive back's full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available to play against the Jaguars on Sunday.

12712.long: The second-year cornerback was injured in the Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals, but the bye came at the right time, and he appears to be ready to go for Sunday's date with the Jaguars. Harris has functioned as Tennessee's slot corner this season, so he figures to see plenty of Parker Washington in Week 10.

11847.short: The Titans placed Williams (groin) on injured reserve Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
11847.long: In a corresponding transaction, Tennessee activated linebacker Dorian Mausi from injured reserve. Williams won't be able to return to game action until Week 14 against the Lions at the earliest. In the meantime, Mausi figures to assume the small role Williams was occupying.

12944.short: The Titans activated Mausi (foot) from injured reserve Monday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
12944.long: Mausi has been on IR since late August with a foot injury, but it now looks like he'll finally be ready to return to game action in Week 10. In 17 regular-season games with Tennessee in 2025, all 341 of his snaps came on special teams.

13288.short: Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that Singleton is "getting better," and the rookie running back could be a candidate to see added opportunities in the second half of the season if lead back Tony Pollard is dealt ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports.
13288.long: A fifth-round pick out of Penn State, Singleton was a healthy inactive for four of the Titans' first eight games prior to a Week 9 bye and has logged more snaps on special teams than offense thus far during his rookie season. However, with the 29-year-old Pollard set to become a free agent after the season and likely not part of the 1-7 Titans' rebuilding effort, playing time could become up for grabs in the backfield if Tennessee receives an appealing trade offer for the veteran. Along with Singleton, Tyjae Spears (knee) and Michael Carter would be vying for reps in the event Pollard is traded, while Julius Chestnut is another option in the backfield but has been utilized almost exclusively on special teams.

4981.short: Titans head coach Robert Saleh confirmed Monday that Ridley was involved in an "unfortunate" interaction over the weekend at Nashville International Airport that is now in the hands of law enforcement, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
4981.long: Though neither the Titans nor the police have publicly shared details pertaining to the incident, Saleh described it as a "very minor miscommunication." Saleh didn't indicate that Ridley's availability for Sunday's game against the Jaguars is in any jeopardy following the incident, though the 31-year-old wideout could be a candidate to get dealt elsewhere ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. Ridley has been limited to six receptions for 91 yards on 13 targets through seven appearances and doesn't look to be a major part of the 1-7 Titans' immediate or long-term plans.

6528.short: Slye hit both field-goal tries and his two extra-point attempts in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.
6528.long: The kicker drilled field goals from 46 and 29 yards out. Slye has only missed one kick this year, a field goal, but the Titans' offense has not been consistent enough to give him ample opportunities on a weekly basis.

12499.short: Ayomanor caught three of five targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.
12499.long: Even with Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Ayomanor's role didn't grow much, as Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm and Chimere Dike combined to see 22 of the team's 39 targets. Through eight games this season, Ayomanor has 13 grabs for 211 yards and a touchdown on 26 targets.

12502.short: Helm caught five of nine targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals.
12502.long: Helm led the team in targets while he was able to register a new career-high 76 receiving yards in the contest. The tight end has now reeled in eight passes over the last two weeks after he caught nine of 13 targets for 60 yards over the first six games of the 2026 campaign. Helm will have a tough test against the Jaguars in Week 10 after the team's bye week in Week 9.

8126.short: Robinson caught six of seven targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He also lost a fumble.
8126.long: Robinson didn't experience a significant change in role in the absence of Carnell Tate (shoulder), as this was the fourth consecutive game in which Robinson notched either six or seven targets. His 57 receiving yards tied a season high, and Robinson scored his third touchdown of the season on a 15-yard catch in the fourth quarter. The Titans took a seven-point lead with 3:46 remaining after a successful two-point conversion following Robinson's TD, but the Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown drive and eventually won in OT to drop the Titans to 1-7. Robinson and the Titans will be on bye in Week 9 before returning to action against the Jaguars in Week 10.

12522.short: Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion.
12522.long: Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

5466.short: Franklin-Myers (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
5466.long: Franklin-Myers drew the questionable tag after ending Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices, and the veteran defensive lineman has been cleared by medical staff to suit up Sunday. He has 14 tackles (six solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through seven regular-season games, but he'll be tasked with a larger role on the defensive line in the absence of Jeffery Simmons, the latter of whom was traded to the Bears on Thursday.

5792.short: Reaves recorded nine tackles (seven solo), one pass defense and one fumble recovery during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
5792.long: Reaves finished Thursday's game second on the Commanders in tackles behind rookie first-round linebacker Sonny Styles (13), and the former jumped on a loose ball caused by Frankie Luvu in the third quarter that stopped the Giants' red zone drive. Reaves has logged at least five stops in each of the first nine games of the regular season, and the veteran safety is up to 62 tackles (35 solo), four pass defenses and one fumble recovery on the year.

8392.short: Cross finished Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants with six tackles (one solo).
8392.long: Cross was one of three Commanders players who played all 65 defensive snaps during Thursday's win. He's posted at least six stops in each of his last three outings, and over that span, he has accumulated 23 tackles (12 solo), three pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.

5580.short: Luvu recorded six tackles (two solo) and a forced fumble during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
5580.long: Luvu stopped the Giants' red zone drive in the third quarter after punching the ball out of the hands of Malik Nabers, and Jeremy Reaves jumped on the loose ball to secure the takeaway for the Commanders. Luvu has played every single snap in each of his last three games, and he has accumulated 51 tackles (21 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery over his last six outings.

13375.short: Styles recorded 13 tackles (five solo) during the Commanders' 24-21 win over the Giants on Thursday.
13375.long: Styles once again led the Commanders in stops while playing every single defensive snap. He has logged exactly 13 tackles in four of his last five games and is up to 80 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games. Styles' 80 combined tackles are third-most among rookies behind Anthony Hill (neck) (82) and Arvell Reese (81).

13968.short: Stevens made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three of his extra-point tries in Thursday's 24-21 win over the Giants.
